Global Conflict Monitor

Updated 11/10/2026 · 05:00 EST · WW3 risk index: 65% (an editorial judgement, not a forecast; see llms.txt)

Breaking: Trump says the Iran war is 'militarily effectively over' and further US strikes are 'quite unlikely' after meeting Qatar's prime minister; Rubio reports no progress in talks and Iran repeats its conditions.

Latest updates

  • Arab News — US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine began in Abu Dhabi, the first in nine months, with the delegations seated opposite each other and US envoys Witkoff and Kushner at the head of the table.
  • The Guardian — US officials said their plan for the Abu Dhabi talks includes a 'long-term security architecture' between Russia and Europe, a possible revived NATO-Russia Council, possible sanctions relief and NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine.
  • Kyiv Independent — German, French, British, Italian and EU officials met Ukraine's and the US delegations in Abu Dhabi outside the three-way format; the Kremlin rejected any European role, and France said European security cannot be negotiated before a ceasefire.
  • Arab News — Trump said after meeting Qatar's prime minister that the Iran war is 'militarily effectively over' and renewed US strikes are 'quite unlikely', while warning the US remains ready; Rubio reported no progress in talks.
  • The Guardian — The US moved refuelling tankers out of RAF Mildenhall over an Iran-linked threat and raised Mildenhall and Lakenheath to FPCON Charlie, the Wall Street Journal reported; it is the second UK base vacated after Fairford.
  • France 24 — France blamed the Revolutionary Guard's Shahid Kaveh cyber unit for October attacks that raised fridge temperatures at hundreds of French supermarkets; prosecutors opened a probe and sought warrants for two officials.
  • Al Jazeera — An attack on the East-West oil pipeline in the Medina region caused a limited fire; Saudi Arabia said operations were unaffected and its defences intercepted missiles fired at Riyadh.
  • Kyiv Independent — A drone killed a worker at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, the IAEA said, a day after the plant lost its only external power line for about 10 hours; a second drone killed a worker at the nearby thermal plant.
  • Kyiv Independent — Russian forces struck the Trypillia thermal power plant near Kyiv; state operator Centrenergo warned of 'extremely serious' consequences as the grid campaign continues before winter.
  • Kyiv Post — Canada sanctioned 38 entities and 24 people linked to Russia's ballistic-missile industry, Russian cyber actors and financial enablers including crypto exchanges.
  • Reuters — China extended its trade truce with the US by two months, keeping a 24% tariff suspended and extending export-control waivers on certain critical minerals and its port-fee suspension to 10 January 2027.
  • SCMP — Lithuania's president confirmed talks on renaming Taiwan's representative office in Vilnius, a move Beijing has sought since 2021; Taiwan said it has no plans to change the name.
  • Al Jazeera — A Houthi missile attack on Riyadh damaged an Aramco office tower in the King Abdullah Financial District; Saudi authorities blamed falling shrapnel and reported no casualties after intercepting missiles at Riyadh and the Eastern Province.
  • The New Arab — CENTCOM set up Task Force Iron Gate, a small team tasked with stopping weapons, dual-use goods and sanctioned materials reaching Iran over land borders and across the Caspian.
  • Reuters — Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two oil tankers hit mines and caught fire on an 'unauthorised' Hormuz route; Reuters could not confirm the claims and Iran suggested the blasts were not US attacks.
  • Euronews — Trump said he expects to meet Putin and Xi at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18-19 November; China says only that it is in communication about a three-leader meeting.
  • Arab News — Regional officials told Reuters a Qatari bridge plan would have the US lift its blockade and release some frozen funds while Iran admits IAEA inspectors, then reopen Hormuz on day two; Iran is reviewing it and the White House declined comment.
  • Kyiv Independent — Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and its region overnight, Zelensky said, closing the Northern Bridge and and, he said, hitting substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants to Kyiv; at least six were injured in Kyiv, and police reported one death in the region.
  • Kyiv Post — The death toll from Russia's 2 November strike on a school used as an aid point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 55, Ukrainian officials said.
  • Arab News — China's foreign ministry said it is 'in communication with relevant parties' about a meeting of Xi, Trump and Putin, possibly at APEC in Shenzhen this month; AP reports nothing is set.

Jul 6 [high] Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Gazprom Neft Omsk refinery — Russia's largest by capacity — overnight at approximately 2,500 km reach, hitting the ELOU-AVT-11 primary refining unit; Ukraine's General Staff separately characterized it as the 9th of Russia's top 11 refineries hit in the 2026 campaign (Ukrainian framing, pending independent inventory reconciliation).
  203. Jul 6 [low] Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense recorded 5 PLA sorties on the July 6 morning update with 3 crossing the median line — third consecutive sub-threshold day continuing the pattern-break from the July 3 peak, with the Bessent-He Lifeng trade lane still silent into a seventh day of the arc.
  204. Jul 6 [moderate] An Israeli drone strike on a vehicle in Nabatieh al-Fawqa in southern Lebanon killed four civilians on July 6 — the deadliest single incident since the June framework — as Hezbollah again held kinetic discipline with no retaliatory salvo and no Beirut target struck.
  205. Jul 6 [critical] China conducted a submarine-launched ballistic-missile test over the Pacific on July 6, confirmed at institutional tier (CNN + CSIS analysis + Washington Post), coinciding with the opening of the annual China-Russia Joint Sea naval exercise. A dummy warhead reportedly landed in the South Pacific — a first-cycle Chinese strategic-force demonstration held for verification yesterday and now cleared.
  206. Jul 7 [low] Taiwan's defense ministry recorded four PLA sorties with three median-line crossings on July 7, a fourth consecutive sub-threshold day that extends the reversion from the July 1-3 surge.
  207. Jul 7 [moderate] The UN Human Rights Council passed a motion condemning Rapid Support Forces violence at El Obeid and opened an urgent inquiry as 28 countries jointly warned of impending atrocities, while the RSF siege continued without a ground assault across the city perimeter.
  208. Jul 7 [high] The US Treasury's OFAC formally revoked Iran General License X and issued a narrow replacement, GL X1, authorizing only a wind-down of existing dealings through July 17 — reversing the 60-day USD-settlement authorization 15 days after issuing it, with no executed Iran-oil sale ever surfacing.
  209. Jul 7 [extreme] Iran's IRGC struck commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on July 7, hitting a Qatari LNG carrier, and the US retaliated against a reported 80-plus Iranian targets while revoking OFAC General License X for Iran oil sales. Trump declared the June framework "over" and Iran threatened a "crushing response," breaking the ten-day US-Iran stand-down. Brent crude spiked about 5% to roughly $78.
  210. Jul 8 [critical] The United States carried out additional strikes on Iranian coastal and IRGC sites — reported to include Sirik, Qeshm and Bandar Abbas around the Strait of Hormuz — a day after its 80-plus-target retaliation, while President Trump declared the June framework "over" and "a waste of time," deepening the collapse of the ten-day stand-down.
  211. Jul 8 [moderate] A multi-day state funeral for Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei — killed in the February 28 opening strike — drew very large crowds across Tehran, Qom, Najaf and Karbala from July 3-9, a delayed ceremonial funeral rather than a new death; his successor Mojtaba Khamenei has led since March.
  212. Jul 8 [high] NATO's Ankara summit on July 7-8 committed EUR70 billion in military equipment, assistance and training for Ukraine across 2026-27, reaffirmed the Article 5 collective-defence pledge, and approved a EUR27 billion investment to modernise allied fuel storage and distribution.
  213. Jul 10 [high] Russia announced a full diesel-export ban through July 31, unveiled by Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak in a televised meeting with President Putin, after Ukrainian drone strikes on July 9 hit oil facilities across several regions and tankers in the Sea of Azov — the refinery campaign's first cabinet-decree export-control conversion beyond the July-1 gasoline ban.
  214. Jul 10 [critical] The US-Iran exchange extended over July 8-9: US forces ran an additional strike round on Iran — corroborated by PBS ("CENTCOM completed a new round of strikes") alongside NPR and CNN — while Iran was reported by NPR, though not independently confirmed, to have fired back at US bases in Gulf Arab states. The IRGC's claim of an 85-target strike on the same Kuwait and Bahrain bases hit in the confirmed late-June exchange stays unverified against a re-dating tell, and Brent eased to about $76 rather than spiking.
  215. Jul 10 [moderate] China's July-6 Pacific submarine-launched ballistic-missile test cleared fresh wire confirmation (USNI News, CSIS, CNN, NPR) during the annual China-Russia Joint Sea exercise; Taiwan air-incursion counts held sub-threshold and the Bessent-He Lifeng trade lane stayed silent.
  216. Jul 11 [critical] An additional US strike round on Iran — roughly 90 targets — firmed at a fresh Al Jazeera dateline, and Trump called the June ceasefire "over" while signaling Washington is still willing to resume talks with Tehran. Iran's IRGC claim of an 85-target strike on the same Kuwait and Bahrain bases hit in late June stays unverified against a re-dating tell, and Brent eased to about $76 rather than spiking.
  217. Jul 13 [critical] The US-Iran exchange re-intensified after a two-day lull: a new US strike wave on Iran and an Iranian counter-strike on US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan were reported on independent Al Jazeera datelines, though every tier-1 Western wire attempt was blocked and the specific '140-site' scale Iran claimed could not be verified.
  218. Jul 14 [high] Iran struck two UAE tankers near the Strait of Hormuz on July 12, killing an Indian crew member and drawing GCC condemnation — the first commercial-shipping fatality of the US-Iran exchange. Coverage described attacks on shipping and a "battle over control" of the waterway, not a formal closure order; Brent climbed to about $87 but stayed below the $90-plus a genuine closure would bring.
  219. Jul 15 [critical] The US struck dozens of Iranian targets in a fresh daytime strike wave dated July 14, a roughly 90-minute CENTCOM operation, as President Trump said strikes would continue "until I say so" and demanded renewed negotiations.
  220. Jul 15 [critical] Iran's cruise-missile strike on two UAE tankers near the Strait of Hormuz is now confirmed by UAE and Gulf outlets — vessels Mombasa and Al Bahyah, one Indian crew member killed and eight injured — upgrading the earlier single-source report; the outlets date the attack July 14.
  221. Jul 15 [high] OFAC's GL X1 wind-down license for Iran oil dealings is set to expire July 17 with no successor announced, and legal analysts confirm the pre-June sanctions regime automatically snaps back on July 18.
  222. Jul 16 [critical] OFAC's GL X1 wind-down licence for Iranian oil and petrochemical dealings expires July 17 at 12:01am EDT with no successor authorisation announced, restoring the full pre-June-22 Iran sanctions regime on July 18.
  223. Jul 18 [critical] The full pre-June US sanctions regime on Iran returned to force July 18 after the wind-down licence expired at 12:01am July 17 with no successor. The restoration required no signature, and the secondary-sanctions threat against Chinese banks and refiners is live again.
  224. Jul 19 [critical] US strikes on Iran ran through a ninth consecutive night by July 20, widening to power facilities and a desalination plant in Hormozgan province, with about 50 people reported killed in July. No pause and no scheduled negotiating round accompanied the escalation.
  225. Jul 19 [high] Iran responded to the strike campaign July 19 with missile and drone attacks on US bases in Gulf states, per Al Jazeera. Iranian state media named an ammunition depot and a Patriot radar site in Kuwait, but no US or Kuwaiti confirmation of specific targets has surfaced.
  226. Jul 20 [high] A Russian strike killed 10 people on a ship near Odesa while Ukraine sent more than 400 drones at Moscow region, wounding at least 10 — Ukraine's largest capital-region raid of the war and a step past its refinery-and-shipping campaign.
  227. Jul 20 [moderate] Andy Burnham became UK prime minister, replacing Keir Starmer, after Labour elected him party leader on July 16 — a change of government in a nuclear-armed NATO member and one of Ukraine’s larger military backers.
  228. Jul 21 [critical] Three US service members were killed July 18-20 — two at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, one in a drone detonation in Iraq — with nearly 100 injured across two weeks of Iranian retaliation. PBS reports 17 US deaths since the war began in February, an aggregate figure not previously carried here.
  229. Jul 21 [critical] US strikes on Iran ran a tenth consecutive night into July 21, hitting military command centers and maritime capabilities. Greek tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz and off Oman as Iran kept pressure on commercial shipping.
  230. Jul 22 [critical] US strikes on Iran ran an eleventh consecutive night while Iranian retaliation widened: Jordan’s military said six Iranian missiles were fired at the kingdom, four intercepted, and Iranian attacks targeted bases in Bahrain. The Pentagon identified a fourth US service member killed, Sgt. Michael Swinton.
  231. Jul 22 [high] Brent crude jumped 3.6% past $94 — its first genuine war-premium spike of the re-escalation — after Secretary Rubio said Iran is "not serious" about peace talks. A reported July 21 settlement of $91.01 had already topped $90, ending the market’s two-week refusal to price the war.
  232. Jul 23 [high] Houthi forces attacked Saudi-linked oil tankers in the southern Red Sea: UKMTO relayed a confirmed strike and fire aboard the Encelia about 70 nautical miles southwest of Al Shuqaiq, while a claimed second hit on the Layla remains unverified. It is the group's first confirmed attack on commercial shipping since the September 2025 pause, converting Monday's blockade warnings into action within 24 hours.
  233. Jul 23 [critical] US strikes on Iran ran a twelfth consecutive night, with CENTCOM targeting maritime capabilities, drone storage and logistics infrastructure. Al Jazeera carried reports of new Iranian retaliatory fire toward Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan, though it is unverified whether this is a second salvo distinct from the July 21-22 attack.
  234. Jul 23 [critical] Iran fired a second, distinct salvo toward Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait on July 23 — Sheikh Isa Air Base and Muwaffaq Salti were named targets — 48 hours after the first six-missile Jordan salvo. Claims the fire extended to Oman and Qatar rest on a single flawed-dateline source and are unverified.
  235. Jul 23 [high] The European Union adopted its 21st Russia sanctions package, adding fourteen Chinese and Hong Kong companies for supplying the war effort; by 31 July Beijing had barred fourteen European companies from receiving Chinese dual-use goods in retaliation. (Backfilled 8 September.)
  236. Jul 24 [critical] US strikes on Iran completed a thirteenth consecutive night, hitting command centers, drone storage and coastal surveillance, as Trump threatened the "biggest strikes yet" and said he is weighing a massive attack. Iranian media reported blasts at Khorramabad, Jask, Ahvaz and Bandar Abbas.
  237. Jul 24 [high] Russia struck a Kyiv arms exhibition with a daytime ballistic missile, killing at least 10 and injuring over 100 — an unusual departure from its night-strike pattern. Overnight, Ukraine sent one of its largest drone barrages of the war (Russia claims 571 intercepted), setting fire to Wildberries e-commerce warehouses near St. Petersburg.
  238. Jul 24 [high] Brent crude crossed $100 a barrel intraday for the first time since May, after a July-23 settlement between $99.17 and $100.69 depending on source. The suspected $86 feed print was confirmed as a contract-rollover artifact; the war premium is holding across a third session.
  239. Jul 25 [critical] US strikes on Iran ran a fourteenth consecutive night, hitting IRGC Navy headquarters in Gilan province and communications infrastructure — a claimed pause failed verification. Trump simultaneously threatened the "biggest strikes yet" and said he "hasn't decided" on major new strikes, calling Tehran "getting serious."
  240. Jul 27 [critical] US strikes on Iran stopped after Trump ordered a hold when an Omani mediation delegation arrived in Tehran, ending fourteen consecutive announced strike nights. A second quiet night is reported with Iran also standing down, though no official pause statement exists from either side.
  241. Jul 28 [high] Netanyahu and Trump met at the White House for the first time since the war began — roughly 80 minutes, no press conference. Netanyahu called it "one of the best we've ever had"; the White House said "productive"; no substance was disclosed.
  242. Jul 30 [critical] US Central Command struck dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets inside Iran, hitting command centres, missile and drone facilities and coastal surveillance sites at Qeshm Island, Ahvaz, Abadan, Bushehr, Kazerun and Farashband. CENTCOM described the two-hour operation as a response to Iranian attacks on US forces.
  243. Jul 30 [critical] A Russian strike on Radushne near Kryvyi Rih killed at least six members of one family, including three children. Zelensky said that as of now it was a North Korean ballistic missile, with examinations to follow — the first reported use of a North Korean missile since August 2025. (Backfilled 8 September.)
  244. Jul 31 [high] The June-26 framework's deadline for Israel to complete its two-pilot-area withdrawal from southern Lebanon arrived with only Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh vacated, and no extension or replacement timetable has been announced as of this update. Israel said days earlier that it would accept no additional withdrawals and would retain freedom of action. The next scheduled talks fall on August 4.
  245. Jul 31 [critical] Iran's military said it struck the US-used Ahmad Al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait with drones. A second account says the drones were shot down, and a third describes Kuwaiti power and water plants being hit. No Kuwaiti or American official is on the record in any of them.
  246. Jul 31 [moderate] A Gaza disarmament agreement was announced under which Hamas would hand weapons to a Palestinian committee over roughly two to three hundred days, conditional on phased Israeli withdrawal and overseen by an international verification commission. Israel has not publicly confirmed it accepts the terms.
  247. Jul 31 [moderate] A federal advisory records malicious cyber actors targeting internet-facing controllers at water and wastewater utilities and causing operational disruptions, and urges operators to take those controllers off the public internet. It names no actor and no country.
  248. Jul 31 [moderate] Kuwait's defence ministry said on 31 July that hostile targets were engaged and destroyed, causing material damage from falling shrapnel and no casualties. The statement names no base and does not acknowledge that anything was struck.
  249. Aug 1 [high] Russia struck Kyiv overnight with ballistic missiles and drones, killing at least nine people and wounding more than thirty. It is the deadliest single attack on the capital in this phase of the campaign.
  250. Aug 2 [high] President Trump said on August 2 that he would "cancel the attack" on Iran, subject to rapidly reaching a deal, naming the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz among the terms. He said negotiations would begin Monday.
  251. Aug 2 [high] Russia and Ukraine traded strikes on August 2 that killed at least fourteen people between them. Ukraine hit the Saratov oil refinery, the Engels strategic airbase, a fuel depot in Kaluga and a warehouse in Samara.
  252. Aug 2 [moderate] No account of the July 30 US target list inside Iran places nuclear infrastructure in it. Two independent descriptions of the strikes name Revolutionary Guard command centres, missile and drone facilities and coastal defence sites across four provinces, including Bushehr, and neither mentions a nuclear facility.
  253. Aug 3 [moderate] Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman said Iran would neither host a delegation nor be a guest of another country “during these days,” declining the round President Trump announced for Monday. Trump described the prospective talks as Iran’s “last chance.”
  254. Aug 3 [high] At least twenty-seven people were reported killed as Russia and Ukraine traded heavy attacks across August 2 and 3, with strikes in Zaporizhzhia, Kryvyi Rih, Krasnodar, Belgorod and Crimea. The count comes from a single report and may include the fourteen recorded here for August 2.
  255. Aug 4 [high] The United States has expended virtually all of its long-range precision missiles — ATACMS and the Precision Strike Missile — during the Iran war, according to sources cited by Reuters. Interceptor stocks are reported heavily drawn down. The White House disputes the characterisation, saying the country holds more munitions than anyone in the world.
  256. Aug 4 [moderate] American officials said an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz could come within days. Treasury Secretary Bessent named Wednesday, Secretary of State Rubio said progress had been made but there was still work to do, and President Trump said all-day talks had been held and warned Iran would be hit very hard if the Strait did not open soon.
  257. Aug 4 [moderate] A projectile sank an Indian-flagged vessel off the coast of Yemen. All fourteen crew were rescued. No party has claimed responsibility, and no maritime authority has attributed the attack.
  258. Aug 4 [moderate] Israeli and Lebanese delegations opened talks in Rome on August 4, the first scheduled session since the withdrawal deadline lapsed on July 31 with a single disputed village vacated and no replacement timetable.
  259. Aug 5 [high] A Russian ballistic-missile attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region killed at least seventeen people and injured forty-four. President Zelensky said interceptors could have saved lives, and Ukrainian accounts report that none of the incoming package was brought down.
  260. Aug 5 [high] Police found a drone carrying an explosive device beside a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport in Germany, and a second flying object struck a cargo plane at the same airport. Germany's interior minister called it a new level of danger. No attribution has been made.
  261. Aug 6 [moderate] Ukraine struck two Russian oil refineries overnight, at Yaroslavl and in Bashkortostan, in what President Zelensky described as a deep-strike drone attack. Ukrainian reporting describes the Yaroslavl plant as among Russia's largest and the seventh top-tier refinery hit this year.
  262. Aug 6 [moderate] An oil tanker reported two explosions while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on August 6, southeast of Kumzar. The crew was reported safe. No party has claimed the incident and no maritime authority has attributed it.
  263. Aug 6 [high] Reuters, citing Ukrainian military intelligence, reported that North Korea has deployed a ballistic-missile unit to Russia's Voronezh region — around 90 personnel attached to the 112th Missile Brigade, with up to 120 short-range ballistic missiles. Neither Moscow nor Pyongyang has confirmed it.
  264. Aug 6 [high] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 21 Chinese military aircraft in the island's air defence identification zone on August 5, including 17 crossings of the Taiwan Strait median line, and 14 aircraft with 6 crossings on August 6; the August 4 report was not retrieved. The last figure this dashboard carried, for August 3, was a single aircraft and no crossings. The readings fall during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang exercises.
  265. Aug 6 [moderate] A sixth consecutive night passed with no reported strikes inside Iran, and the order against Iranian refineries and power plants remained unexecuted. President Trump publicly denied that the United States is running low on munitions, days after reporting that it had expended virtually all of its long-range precision missiles.
  266. Aug 6 [moderate] The United States removed the Iraqi carrier Fly Baghdad from its sanctions list, unblocking the airline and delisting two of its aircraft, though its owner remains designated. The airline had been sanctioned over alleged links to Iran's Revolutionary Guard.
  267. Aug 6 [high] Houthi forces killed Saudi-backed Yemeni government troops in the heaviest ground fighting since the 2022 truce, with one established outlet reporting 58 dead and the government confirming more than thirty. Reporting describes a risk that Yemen's civil war reignites.
  268. Aug 6 [high] Iran is seeking to bar United States and Israeli ships from the Strait of Hormuz and to charge all other vessels a transit toll, according to NPR. No Iranian order or fee schedule has been published, and attempts to reach Iran's foreign ministry and its parliament's news agency to check the proposal's status did not resolve.
  269. Aug 7 [moderate] Ukraine struck a Wildberries logistics centre in Yekaterinburg, roughly 2,000 kilometres from the front line, with a large fire reported. It is the second strike on the Russian e-commerce group's warehouses in four days.
  270. Aug 7 [moderate] A seventh consecutive night passed with no reported strikes inside Iran, and the order against Iranian refineries and power plants remained unexecuted. President Trump said the war had "got to end pretty soon" and that Iran could not "go on much longer," while expressing optimism about a Strait of Hormuz agreement.
  271. Aug 7 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry reported 10 Chinese military aircraft and 6 median-line crossings for August 7, a third consecutive daily decline from the 21 aircraft recorded on August 5. The ministry's previously missing August 4 record was retrieved and shows 6 aircraft, placing the rise into the island's annual exercises as gradual rather than abrupt.
  272. Aug 7 [moderate] Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are expected to sign a joint defence agreement in Jeddah covering exercises, technology transfer, defence industry and intelligence sharing. Nothing has been signed: the Turkish and Pakistani foreign ministries and NATO's newsroom all resolved and carry no statement on it.
  273. Aug 7 [high] Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca, committing each state to treat an armed attack on any one of the three as an attack on all. Turkish officials described the pact as defensive, directed at no particular actor and open to other regional countries.
  274. Aug 8 [moderate] The US Treasury sanctioned a Dubai-based cryptocurrency exchange and an Iran-based tether operation over a reported four-billion-dollar sanctions-evasion pipeline serving the Revolutionary Guards, on the same day the State Department published two Iran financial-pressure releases.
  275. Aug 8 [high] Ukraine's defence ministry said it intercepted 29 of 195 Russian ballistic missiles in July as air-defence shortages deepened, an interception rate near 15%. Ukrainian reporting put the overnight package at six Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 151 drones, with none of the ballistic missiles intercepted. Ukraine separately struck Russian oil refineries in Samara Oblast and Krasnodar Krai.
  276. Aug 8 [critical] Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca containing a mutual-defence clause, under which an armed attack on any one of the three states is to be regarded as an attack on all. Turkey's foreign ministry and NATO's newsroom have said nothing about it.
  277. Aug 8 [moderate] An eighth consecutive night passed with no reported strikes inside Iran, and the order against Iranian refineries and power plants remained unexecuted. Iran said the Strait of Hormuz accord is awaiting approval from its top security council, while a US official said a deal was expected soon.
  278. Aug 8 [high] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 14 Chinese military aircraft and 11 crossings of the Taiwan Strait median line for August 8, alongside 6 navy vessels and 8 official ships. The count rose from 10 the previous day, ending a three-day decline, with median-line crossings nearly doubling.
  279. Aug 8 [high] The US Senate passed a sweeping Russian energy sanctions bill in a final-passage vote of 86 to 11 on August 7, targeting buyers of Russian energy and named as Vote 224 in the Senate's own roll-call record. The measure still requires House passage and presidential signature.
  280. Aug 8 [high] Russian missile strikes near Kyiv killed at least three people including a child and injured seven, in a further overnight attack on the capital region. Wider reporting put the night's toll across Ukraine at twelve killed and 81 injured.
  281. Aug 8 [high] Houthi attacks killed at least ten more Yemeni government personnel as the group targeted the oil-rich Marib region, days after the heaviest ground fighting since the 2022 truce. The UN warned Yemen faces a return to full-scale civil war.
  282. Aug 9 [high] Iran issued a list of demands for reopening the Strait of Hormuz: an end to strikes in Iran, Lebanon, Yemen, Iraq and the Palestinian territories, the withdrawal of US naval and air forces, war reparations, the release of frozen assets and the lifting of sanctions. Tehran also said any agreement would not by itself reopen the waterway.
  283. Aug 9 [high] Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said a fire at the Aramco facility in Jizan had been extinguished and did not say what caused it. The Houthis separately claimed they had struck the refinery with a drone. Neither the EIA nor the IEA records any Saudi refining outage.
  284. Aug 9 [critical] The United Arab Emirates says an Iranian missile struck a vessel affiliated with its state oil company ADNOC as it transited the Strait of Hormuz, with no injuries reported. The UAE foreign ministry condemned what it called a hostile Iranian attack. It is the first kinetic incident between Iran and the UAE in this war.
  285. Aug 9 [high] Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on two Russian oil refineries — Ilsky in Krasnodar Krai and Syzran in Samara Oblast — and on a Black Sea drilling rig. Kyiv separately said it had struck twelve Russian shadow-fleet vessels in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov over the past week.
  286. Aug 10 [high] President Trump said the United States is “low-keying it” with Iran and only “semi-negotiating,” describing a shift from military strikes to economic pressure as Iran's economy deteriorates. He did not say strikes had been paused, and the White House public record carries no statement on it.
  287. Aug 10 [high] The reported death toll from the Ukrainian drone strike on the Taneco complex at Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan rose to at least thirteen. Seven of the dead were Uzbek nationals working at the site, according to Uzbekistan's consulate, and a child was also among them.
  288. Aug 10 [high] UN peacekeepers in Lebanon counted 455 Israeli projectiles and 97 airspace violations over a single weekend, with 229 on Saturday alone — the highest one-day figure since 21 June — and reported two Israeli tanks firing near a UN position.
  289. Aug 10 [high] Iran appointed Mohsen Rezaei, who commanded the Revolutionary Guards from 1981 to 1997, as secretary of its Supreme National Security Council — the body Tehran says must approve any Strait of Hormuz arrangement, seven days before the memorandum's deadline.
  290. Aug 10 [high] Houthi missile and drone attacks on the government-held Yemeni port of al-Makha killed ten people, seven of them military, a day after strikes on the same port killed eleven. The Houthi military spokesman claimed both.
  291. Aug 10 [high] Ukrainian drones struck the Taneco refinery and petrochemical complex at Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan, more than 1,200 kilometres from the border. Russian regional authorities said twelve people were killed, a figure no independent source has yet confirmed. Moscow said it intercepted 456 drones overnight.
  292. Aug 10 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded one Chinese military aircraft, one median-line crossing, nine navy vessels and eleven official ships for 10 August, a second consecutive single-digit day. The Han Kuang exercises run to 14 August and Typhoon Dolphin was still closing regional ports.
  293. Aug 11 [high] A drone strike set fire to a storage tank at Libya's Zawiya refinery, the country's largest operating refinery at about 120,000 barrels a day, and the National Oil Corporation warned it could declare force majeure if attacks continue. Nobody claimed the strike. A car bomb separately killed eastern Libya's military intelligence chief.
  294. Aug 11 [high] President Trump said the United States would require compensation from Iran covering roughly fifty years of damages, including the deaths of US service members, and said the Strait of Hormuz is open with the US Navy in control. Iran's Supreme National Security Council said the same day that the Strait stays closed until Washington corrects its behaviour.
  295. Aug 11 [critical] A Russian ballistic-missile strike on the Zaporizhstal steel plant killed at least six workers on their way to a shelter — seven by later counts — and wounded dozens, shutting the plant; at least twelve people died across Ukraine overnight. Zelensky said the city was struck with North Korean ballistic missiles, Zircons and guided aerial bombs. (Backfilled 8 September.)
  296. Aug 12 [critical] Ukraine damaged four Russian warships in a single night at Novorossiysk, the Black Sea Fleet port Russia had moved its ships to for safety — two Kalibr-carrying frigates, a small missile ship and a patrol vessel.
  297. Aug 12 [high] President Trump said the United States will “keep” the Strait of Hormuz, hardening a position that four days earlier described the waterway as merely open and under US Navy control. Iran's stance that the Strait stays closed until Washington changes its behaviour is unchanged, and the memorandum's sixty days run out the following weekend.
  298. Aug 12 [critical] Israel's defence minister Israel Katz said the army is “here to stay” in security zones in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza and had been instructed to prepare for a long-term presence. The United States publicly responded that a permanent presence in south Lebanon is not consistent with the commitments made in the framework.
  299. Aug 13 [critical] Russian strikes hit major grain export terminals at Ukraine's Black Sea ports, and reporting describes a blockade of the ports that threatens global grain supplies. Ukraine has cut its export forecast for the coming season.
  300. Aug 13 [high] President Putin visited the Kuril Islands, seized from Japan at the end of the Second World War, in the first such visit by a Russian president. Japan summoned Russia's ambassador, and its prime minister called the visit unacceptable.
  301. Aug 13 [high] The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, called an Israeli settler siege of an American Palestinian family's home in the West Bank village of Qusra a horrific act of terror. Israel sent additional troops to the village while the settlers remained.
  302. Aug 13 [high] The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission recorded at least 437 civilians killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine in July — the highest monthly death toll since May 2022, and a sharp rise over both the previous month and the same month last year.
  303. Aug 13 [high] The United Nations envoy told the Security Council that Yemen faces a more serious risk of returning to large-scale conflict than at any point since the 2022 truce, after Houthi ground offensives at Marib, al-Makha and Taiz.
  304. Aug 13 [moderate] The White House said more than forty countries — among them Japan, South Korea, Canada and Mexico — have helped China evade US tariffs by routing goods through third countries.
  305. Aug 13 [high] Poland detained a Russian man over an alleged Kremlin plot to assassinate a US-Ukrainian dual national in Warsaw. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it the first attempt of its kind on NATO territory.
  306. Aug 13 [high] Iraq's government said the 30 September deadline for ending the US-led coalition's military presence is final, and officials said American forces are on track to complete the pullout by that date.
  307. Aug 14 [high] A replacement aircraft carrier is heading toward the Middle East after reports of deteriorating conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, deployed more than 250 days. A senator has pressed the Navy for answers on the deployment's length.
  308. Aug 14 [high] NATO fighters shot down a drone over Latvia's north-eastern Balvi region, the second such incident in two months. Latvia's defence ministry did not identify the drone by type.
  309. Aug 14 [high] The Treasury secretary said the United States will roll out an unprecedented plan for Iran's economic isolation next week, describing economic pressure and a naval blockade as a deliberate pair. It is the first time Washington has attached a timetable to what replaces the strikes that stopped a fortnight ago.
  310. Aug 14 [moderate] Israel's prime minister called the United Kingdom "the Islamic Republic of Britain" and joked it would be the first such state with nuclear weapons. London called the remarks completely unacceptable.
  311. Aug 14 [high] President Trump said he will declare the Strait of Hormuz "a territory of the United States," speaking at a police academy event in New York; one report noted it was unclear whether he was serious. No United States government channel carries the claim.
  312. Aug 14 [high] Russia shut the Sheskharis oil export terminal at Novorossiysk after a Ukrainian drone attack, citing threat warnings and storage capacity. It is the first reported export stoppage from the campaign against the port.
  313. Aug 14 [high] An analysis of North Korean KN-23 missiles fired at Ukraine found their miss distance fell from 500 to 1,500 metres in 2024 to 50 to 100 metres from February 2025, citing Ukraine's intelligence chief that Russian missile experts made technical modifications; the analysis attributes the gain to restored satellite navigation and disputes that Russia analysed combat telemetry. (Backfilled 8 September.)
  314. Aug 15 [high] Iran's foreign minister said no decision has been taken on returning to talks with the United States, and that messages passed through Qatar and Pakistan do not amount to negotiations.
  315. Aug 15 [critical] Israeli strikes killed eleven in southern Lebanon — seven at Ansar and four at Deir al-Zahrani, among them three children and two women, with 19 wounded. The Israeli military said it hit Hezbollah sites after an attack on its troops.
  316. Aug 16 [high] Ukraine launched roughly 600 drones at the Moscow region overnight, damaging a Wildberries warehouse, while Russian strikes across Ukraine killed seven and injured 51, including at a steel plant at Kryvyi Rih.
  317. Aug 16 [moderate] Romania's defence ministry said an aerial target entered national airspace at 04:44 from the direction of Moldova, about 24 kilometres north of Galati. Its statement does not attribute the target to any state, identify it by type, or say what became of it.
  318. Aug 16 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 11 Chinese military aircraft, 7 median-line crossings, 8 navy vessels and 2 official ships for 16 August, up from four aircraft the day before.
  319. Aug 16 [moderate] Israel struck southern Lebanon for a second consecutive day and families were reported fleeing north, with Defence Minister Israel Katz vowing to settle scores. No toll has been reported for the second day.
  320. Aug 16 [high] Ukrainian strikes killed at least six people in Russia's Belgorod region, according to Russian regional authorities, on the same day Russian strikes across Ukraine killed seven and injured 51.
  321. Aug 16 [high] Iran's army commander-in-chief, Major General Amir Hatami, announced a reward of five billion tomans — about $30,000 — for killing or capturing an American soldier, according to Iranian state media. The announcement was framed as part of a military reorganisation ordered by the Supreme Leader.
  322. Aug 16 [high] Jared Kushner met Hamas's political leader Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo, alongside Egyptian and Qatari officials, to press Hamas disarmament and an end to its role governing Gaza. Kushner flew to Israel the following day to meet Prime Minister Netanyahu.
  323. Aug 17 [high] The US-Iran memorandum's sixty days lapsed with no published text, no fee schedule, no venue and no negotiating round either government confirms attending. Neither government marked the expiry, and a federal document search returns no result mentioning the Strait of Hormuz since 1 August.
  324. Aug 17 [high] President Trump ordered the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, saying they are costly and send the wrong signal to North Korea. Neither the Pentagon nor South Korea's defence ministry has published confirmation that any exercise changed.
  325. Aug 18 [high] A commercial vessel was struck by what a maritime authority called an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz early on 18 August, about 23 nautical miles north-east of Al Khasab. The engine room was damaged and one crew casualty was reported, and the Omani coastguard assisted. No party has claimed responsibility.
  326. Aug 18 [high] Russian strikes killed at least ten people in Kharkiv overnight, and President Zelensky said Ukraine would respond. Ukraine sent hundreds of drones at the Moscow region in the same window, and Russian air defences were reported to have shot down more than 180 of them.
  327. Aug 18 [moderate] The IAEA's director general said several tons of natural uranium metal were found at an undisclosed Syrian site and will be placed under international safeguards. Natural uranium is unenriched, and placing it under safeguards moves the material into inspection rather than out of it.
  328. Aug 18 [moderate] The United States designated the International Criminal Court's president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye over the court's investigations of Israeli officials. The court said the measures undermine the rule of law.
  329. Aug 18 [high] Israel struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase in Syria's Idlib province, saying it acted to prevent a Turkish deployment there. Turkey's foreign ministry published a statement on the attack and called the Israeli account a frivolous allegation. A named American envoy called the strike an unnecessary escalation, and no operational American step accompanied the words.
  330. Aug 19 [high] The United Arab Emirates halted all trade, commercial exchange and financial transactions with Iran, announced by the foreign ministry's director of strategic communications on the ministry's own channel. It is the first economic measure a Gulf partner has taken against Tehran independently of any American framework.
  331. Aug 19 [high] The UAE says Iran fired two missiles at it, both of which fell in the sea. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman called the allegation a false-flag operation, and no independent source has corroborated that any launch took place.
  332. Aug 19 [high] South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff announced that the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise has been shortened by six days at Washington's request, and Defence Minister Ahn acknowledged the change to reporters. It is the first command-level confirmation after two days in which US Forces Korea, the Pentagon, Indo-Pacific Command and Seoul's own ministry published nothing at all.
  333. Aug 19 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded twenty Chinese military aircraft, fifteen of them crossing the median line, plus seven navy vessels and six official ships, in ministry record 87490. The previous day's record 87447 showed five aircraft and three crossings.
  334. Aug 19 [high] Ukrainian authorities put the toll from Russian attacks at seventeen killed and fifty-three injured across the country over the past day, including a drone strike on a minibus in Kherson. Russian regional officials reported nine killed and twenty-three injured in Belgorod and one killed in Astrakhan from Ukrainian drone attacks.
  335. Aug 19 [high] A US defence official said the department had substantially reduced the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise on the direction of the President and the Secretary of War, with some live-training events cancelled or converted to simulations. It is the first American confirmation of the change, two days after South Korea announced it; the official was not named and no US command issued a statement.
  336. Aug 20 [high] Australia summoned Israel's ambassador hours after Israel declined a criminal investigation into the killing of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom. It is the first formal diplomatic instrument a US ally has used against another US partner in this war.
  337. Aug 20 [high] Israel's military opened a criminal investigation into the killing of Hind Rajab and the paramedics sent to reach her, and confirmed its soldiers fired at the vehicle, reversing a standing denial. The incident dates to an earlier phase of the war; the investigation is the new development.
  338. Aug 20 [high] Russian missiles and drones struck Kyiv shortly after midnight on 20 August, killing at least fifteen people and injuring about forty, according to the mayor and the president. A children's hospital was damaged, and a later strike the same day cut hot water in two districts.
  339. Aug 20 [high] More than two hundred thousand people were newly displaced in Sudan's Kordofan region as fighting between the army and the Rapid Support Forces intensified, with thousands reaching El Obeid.
  340. Aug 21 [high] Israel re-established a West Bank settlement closed more than twenty years ago, and advanced tenders for the E1 project, in the face of mounting international objection.
  341. Aug 21 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded zero Chinese military aircraft around the island in the twenty-four hours to 21 August, against twenty two days earlier. Seven Chinese navy vessels were still present, the same number as before, so the air activity stopped and the naval activity did not.
  342. Aug 21 [high] President Zelensky confirmed a Ukrainian drone strike on the Lukoil refinery at Perm, roughly 1,500 kilometres from Ukraine and among the deepest targets of the campaign.
  343. Aug 21 [moderate] China's foreign ministry said it rejects sanctions and pressure tactics and will not change its policy toward Iran, answering the American campaign that names consequences for countries trading with Tehran. It is the first on-record refusal by a named target of that campaign.
  344. Aug 21 [high] Fuel rationing spread to Moscow and St Petersburg as Russian refiners capped purchases per customer, and Russia began importing petrol. Reporting ties the shortages directly to the Ukrainian strike campaign on refineries.
  345. Aug 21 [high] Eleven governments — Britain, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Canada, Norway, Australia, New Zealand, Sweden and Belgium — signed a joint statement condemning Israel's E1 settlement project in the occupied West Bank. The statement was published on the British and French governments' own sites.
  346. Aug 21 [high] Russian strikes across Ukraine killed at least six people and injured seventy-seven, with a residential building in Sumy hit in what Ukrainian officials called deliberate targeting.
  347. Aug 21 [critical] A Russian drone strike on a crowded shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih killed at least sixteen people and injured about 130. A second strike roughly thirty minutes later hit the rescue workers who had arrived for the first. The European Union's foreign policy chief called the attack terror by design.
  348. Aug 21 [moderate] Turkey moved to seek an Interpol red notice for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over a Gaza flotilla case. Turkey's own foreign ministry site carries no statement about it, and there is no indication Interpol has accepted the request.
  349. Aug 21 [high] President Trump said he views the Strait of Hormuz as American territory. Direct checks of the White House actions page and the Federal Register on 22 August, both of which answered normally and one of which returned 308 unrelated documents as a control, found no United States government page carrying any such claim.
  350. Aug 22 [high] Iran's new national security chief said neighbouring states that join the American economic campaign will be treated as enemies. It is the first time Tehran has aimed the threat at the Gulf rather than at Washington, four days after the United Arab Emirates halted trade with Iran.
  351. Aug 23 [moderate] A direct check of the Federal Register found three Canada tariff proclamations dated 23 July and one Canada document published this month — a temporary suspension of those same duties. The fifty-percent rate and the twenty-billion-dollar figure reported this week appear on no page that could be opened.
  352. Aug 23 [moderate] Ten days after Washington declared an economic campaign to isolate Iran, a search of the federal record returned two Iran documents, neither of them the campaign, against a control query returning twenty-nine. The authority behind the ten designations announced on 20 August is still unread; Treasury and its sanctions office did not answer on four attempts.
  353. Aug 23 [moderate] An Iran-linked cyberattack took a small British power generator offline for four days, according to reporting first carried by the Telegraph. No United Kingdom government page confirms it, no Iranian group has been named for this operation, and the plant has not been identified.
  354. Aug 24 [moderate] Britain's prime minister arrived in Kyiv for Ukraine's Independence Day, saying he would share long-range missile component designs for assembly in Ukraine. No British government publication carries the offer yet. Six Nordic and Baltic leaders were there with him, and the European Union approved new defence loans the same day.
  355. Aug 24 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry has now recorded four consecutive daily windows with almost no Chinese military aircraft around the island — none, three, none and two, against twenty on 19 August. Chinese navy ships stayed at seven to eight throughout. The air activity stopped and the naval presence did not change.
  356. Aug 24 [moderate] Eleven days after Washington declared a campaign to isolate Iran economically, and a day after the Treasury secretary called it an economic D-Day, the federal record holds no sanctions office document published since 18 August — against a control query returning 469 documents. The White House actions page carries ten items and none concern Iran.
  357. Aug 24 [high] A proclamation published today suspends the additional duties on Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy and motor vehicles — effective 12:01 a.m. eastern on 22 August, the same moment they were due to begin. The imposing proclamations authorised duties of up to fifty percent under section 338. Both the rate and the suspension are in the federal record.
  358. Aug 24 [moderate] South Korea disclosed that the United States has cancelled the Ssangyong amphibious exercise. The Marine Corps notified Seoul in June that force availability would be constrained by the Iran war, so the decision predates its disclosure. It follows Ulchi Freedom Shield being shortened by six days on 19 August.
  359. Aug 24 [high] The Secretary of State authorised the formal rescission of Syria's designation as a state sponsor of terrorism, at the end of a mandatory forty-five-day congressional notification period. Syria's president welcomed it publicly the same day. It lands alongside Syrian and Israeli delegations meeting in Jordan under American mediation.
  360. Aug 24 [high] The President sent a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, starting a ninety-day review after which it takes effect unless Congress objects. The thirty-year accord would let American firms export reactor technology, and Trump has said approval is subject to Riyadh joining the Abraham Accords. Saudi Arabia says it will not normalise with Israel without a path to a Palestinian state.
  361. Aug 24 [high] Britain approved the release of classified Storm Shadow and SCALP missile technology to Ukraine, authorising the manufacturer MBDA to share component data so a production line can be established in Ukraine with French cooperation by the end of the year. The announcement came during the prime minister's first visit to Kyiv.
  362. Aug 25 [high] A ballistic missile struck the Saudi national carrier's tanker Amzan about 63 nautical miles west of Yanbu, starting a fire aboard and sending nearby ships out of the area. Bahri confirmed the incident and said all crew were safe; the British maritime authority recorded a tanker struck by an unknown projectile. A Houthi military spokesman claimed the strike; no Saudi authority has commented.
  363. Aug 25 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry logged a fifth consecutive daily record at or near zero Chinese military aircraft around the island — record 87551 shows none, against twenty on 19 August. Naval vessels held at seven across the entire run. One instrument of pressure has been withdrawn and the other left exactly in place.
  364. Aug 25 [high] Ukraine struck the Afipsky refinery in Russia's Krasnodar Krai, forcing the plant to shut down. A Russian drone hit a residential building in central Chernihiv, injuring at least twenty people including three children, and Ukrainian drones destroyed a second MiG-29 in two days at the Millerovo airbase.
  365. Aug 25 [moderate] Turkey's Interpol request concerns the May 2026 Global Sumud Flotilla, was filed by its Justice Ministry, and names thirty-seven Israeli officials on charges of genocide, crimes against humanity and torture. On 21 August this board declined a claim of that shape and identified the matter as a 2010 flotilla case. The refusal was right about the evidence then available and the counter-identification was wrong.
  366. Aug 25 [moderate] Canada announced retaliatory tariffs on about 27.6 billion dollars of American goods, effective 8 September, and raised its duties on American steel and aluminium from twenty-five to fifty percent. It follows the collapse of trade talks and the President's plan to tax Canadian cars, trucks, parts and steel at fifty percent from January 2027.
  367. Aug 26 [moderate] The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces announced their dissolution and integration into Syria's national military, their commander Mazloum Abdi speaking from the presidential palace in Damascus. Turkey said the step would help Syrian unity.
  368. Aug 26 [high] The Treasury's sanctions office has indefinitely suspended five general licences under the Iranian sanctions regulations, effective 24 August, saying the step aligns the rules with a change in American foreign policy toward Iran. It is the first piece of the economic campaign to appear in the federal record, eleven days after it was announced. It names no company, bank or vessel.
  369. Aug 26 [high] Iran's deputy foreign minister said Tehran and Muscat have agreed a temporary shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, about seven miles wide, whose entry and part of whose exit run through Iranian territorial waters. He added that Iran does not regard the Strait as open. In June, Oman and the International Maritime Organization announced an American-backed corridor along the Omani coast instead.
  370. Aug 26 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry logged a seventh consecutive day at or near zero Chinese military aircraft — records 87552 and 87556 both show none. The naval count, unmoved at seven throughout the run, fell to six.
  371. Aug 26 [high] Russian attacks killed at least four people and injured ninety-five across Ukraine, and a first-person-view drone struck rescue workers responding to an earlier strike in Kramatorsk — a second attack timed to hit the people sent to help.
  372. Aug 26 [high] The sixty entities designated in the 24 August Iran package became readable: about twenty Hong Kong and mainland-Chinese logistics, technology and shipping companies, Iranian ministries including intelligence and defence, and firms across Singapore, Malaysia, France, the UK, Greece and the Marshall Islands. No Chinese bank is on the list.
  373. Aug 26 [high] OFAC's sectoral determination and two new general licences were retrieved in full a day before their Federal Register publication. The determination formally extends sanctions to Iran's aviation, digital-asset, gold, shipping and technology sectors, effective 24 August. The licences reveal that the five suspended authorisations were all people-to-people channels — including personal remittances to and from Iran — now in wind-down until 8 September.
  374. Aug 26 [moderate] Russia's defence minister proposed a five-year military cooperation plan with North Korea running from 2027 to 2031. The first road bridge across the Tumen River between the two countries is nearly finished, with an opening targeted for early September.
  375. Aug 26 [high] Hungary designated Russia a threat to Hungary, Europe and the global order in an official gazette instruction, and stated it condemns Russian aggression and supports Ukraine's sovereignty. Peter Magyar's government, which replaced Viktor Orban after the 12 April election, had earlier lifted a two-year veto on the European Peace Facility, releasing 6.6 billion euros in Ukraine reimbursements.
  376. Aug 27 [high] Iran and Oman issued a joint foreign-ministry statement on a temporary Strait of Hormuz corridor and said they would clear mines from the waterway. Navigation rights, jurisdiction and costs are still being negotiated. Oil fell for a third session on the day of the announcement.
  377. Aug 27 [high] The suspension of American duties on Canadian drinks, dairy and vehicles lasted three days and lapsed on 25 August with no extension published, so duties of up to fifty percent are again in force. Canada's own retaliatory tariffs on about 27.6 billion dollars of American goods take effect on 8 September.
  378. Aug 27 [moderate] The Treasury's sanctions office published two more Iran general licences. One winds down the operations of a named French refining company through 23 October; the other requires every remaining humanitarian, educational and personal-remittance activity to be concluded by 8 September, with any payment to a blocked person routed into a blocked account.
  379. Aug 27 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry logged an eighth consecutive day with no Chinese military aircraft detected around the island, record 87573 stating that none was found. The naval count rose to nine warships, the highest of the run.
  380. Aug 28 [high] Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, set out five conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz: an end to the regional war, a corridor arrangement routing vessels through a middle channel, an end to the American blockade of Iranian ports, compensation for war damage, and sanctions relief. He said the United States must act first.
  381. Aug 28 [moderate] Chad accused Sudan of carrying out an air strike near their shared border that killed 12 people at a fuel market. Sudan has not responded. It is the first allegation in this record of direct state-on-state military action between the two, in a war the board has carried as internal.
  382. Aug 28 [moderate] The United States, South Korea and Japan will hold the Freedom Edge trilateral exercise from 7 to 11 September, in waters off Jeju. The announcement cites North Korean pressure on Washington as the reason, without specifying what that pressure consists of. It is the first trilateral exercise announced since the Ulchi Freedom Shield drill was cut from eleven days to five.
  383. Aug 28 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded no Chinese military aircraft around the island for a ninth consecutive day, in record 87621 covering 27 to 28 August. The naval count fell back to seven warships from nine the day before.
  384. Aug 28 [high] Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz averaged about five vessels a day between 15 July and 23 August, against roughly 100 a day before the war — a fall of about 95 percent, with crude shipments at 2.2 million barrels a day. The figure comes from the tracking firm Kpler and is a floor: the same report says remaining vessels sail under naval escort or with their transponders switched off.
  385. Aug 28 [high] Ukrainian drones targeted Moscow and struck the Slavneft-YANOS refinery at Yaroslavl overnight, setting at least two fires on the plant. Moscow's mayor said air defences destroyed two drones heading for the capital. Casualty reports for the Yaroslavl region conflict: one outlet reports one killed and 27 injured, while the regional governor reported none.
  386. Aug 28 [moderate] The State Department published a sanctions action naming a Bank Melli manager in Dubai and a Hong Kong trading company, together with a proposed rule to cut the Egyptian bank Banque Misr off from correspondent banking in the United Arab Emirates.
  387. Aug 28 [moderate] Israeli aircraft killed three Palestinians in Jenin, the first Israeli air strike in the occupied West Bank since February 2025. The military named one of the dead as a Hamas commander in the city.
  388. Aug 28 [high] Trump announced what he called the biggest oil deal in world history, saying the United States would take control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan reserves at no cost to taxpayers, under an agreement with interim president Delcy Rodríguez. No instrument has reached the federal record: a Federal Register query for Venezuela covering 27 to 29 August returned nothing, and the White House's own news index carried no item on it.
  389. Aug 28 [high] The International Maritime Organization said at least 70 attacks on international shipping near the Strait of Hormuz have been verified and 19 seafarers killed, and that up to 400 ships carrying about 6,000 seafarers have been unable to depart safely since the war began. It is the first institutional count of the trapped shipping population.
  390. Aug 29 [moderate] The United States Justice Department narrowed its account of a Chinese state-linked hacking campaign, saying agencies including the Senate, the Federal Reserve and NASA were targeted rather than all compromised, and that the NASA intrusion did not succeed.
  391. Aug 29 [moderate] A fourth vessel has been hijacked off Somalia since April, with ransom demands reported up to 10 million dollars, in a resurgence attributed to naval resources drawn away by the war with Iran.
  392. Aug 29 [high] Zelensky said Ukraine had been briefed by the United States on the Moscow meetings, the first account of a channel neither government had described. “Today we received information from the American side about the meetings in Moscow that took place these past days,” he said.
  393. Aug 29 [critical] The Russian strike outside Kyiv killed 38 people and injured 20, with four missing. The site was a Ukrainian military ammunition depot at Myla, hit at about 20:10 on 28 August, and it was the secondary detonations that destroyed the surrounding houses. Some 381 people, including 59 children, were evacuated.
  394. Aug 29 [high] The Israeli military said a strike on the Shuhada al-Aqsa hospital compound at Deir al-Balah killed a Hamas commander. The hospital reported three injured near a maternity warehouse; another outlet reported three killed. The claim that a commander was the target is not independently corroborated.
  395. Aug 29 [high] The Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant had been entirely without off-site power for over a week as of 29 August, running on emergency diesel generators with about ten days of fuel. It is the twenty-seventh such blackout since 2022. The IAEA was negotiating a local ceasefire to allow line repairs. The status since has not been established here.
  396. Aug 30 [high] Ukrainian forces struck the Kirishi refinery in Leningrad Oblast and an airbase at Yeysk overnight, according to Ukrainian reporting. Kirishi is the fourth named Russian refinery hit in six days, after Afipsky, NORSI and Slavneft-YANOS.
  397. Aug 30 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded three Chinese military aircraft around the island in record 87626, covering 29 to 30 August, ending ten consecutive days at zero. All three crossed the median line. The ministry counted eight navy vessels and five other Chinese government vessels.
  398. Aug 30 [high] Ukraine's president said the first strike at Myla hit a military ammunition depot and that regulations bar storing ammunition near homes, promising "appropriate conclusions". The prime minister called making the same mistake in the fifth year of the invasion "criminal negligence". No inquiry has been announced.
  399. Aug 31 [extreme] United States Central Command says its forces bombed two Iranian Revolutionary Guard rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. It is the first reported American strike on Iranian territory in about a month, ending the pause this dashboard has been counting since late July.
  400. Aug 31 [critical] Iran said it had attacked American bases in Jordan and military targets at the al-Minhad airbase in the United Arab Emirates in reply to the Larak Island strike. The Emirati defence ministry rejected the claim that al-Minhad was targeted, and no Jordanian government page could be reached to confirm or deny the Jordanian half.
  401. Aug 31 [high] The United States Treasury says the Egyptian state bank Banque Misr's Emirati branches processed about 1.8 billion dollars for 103 companies it links to Iran between January 2024 and June 2026, and that its financial-crimes bureau has proposed a rule cutting those branches off from American correspondent banking. The Emirati central bank has ordered an examination of the branches.
  402. Aug 31 [high] Russia says its Africa Corps helped Niger's government put down the mutiny at Niamey, after the junta asked for assistance. Moscow's ambassador made the statement; it is the first time in this war's record that a Russian paramilitary force has been described as operationally decisive inside a Sahel state.
  403. Aug 31 [high] A Ukrainian strike on Belgorod killed two people, including a sixteen-year-old, and injured sixteen, damaging an Ozon warehouse and a thermal power plant, Russian regional authorities said. It is the second Ozon site struck in three days and the same operator, not a third.
  404. Sep 1 [critical] A Russian missile and drone attack on Kyiv struck a railway depot and killed at least twelve people, including six railway workers, on the sixth consecutive night of the barrage. It is the deadliest night of the current campaign against the capital.
  405. Sep 1 [high] Ukrainian drones damaged Russia's Ust-Luga port on the Baltic, the regional governor said. It extends the deep-strike campaign from refineries to a major export terminal on Russia's northwestern seaboard.
  406. Sep 1 [high] The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit convened at Bishkek with Russia's and China's presidents and Iran's president attending. India's prime minister publicly urged Vladimir Putin to move from an endless war to an end to the war, and Iran's president offered talks with Washington.
  407. Sep 1 [high] Europe protested the United States decision to seat Russia's finance minister at the Group of Twenty finance meeting in North Carolina, his first in-person attendance since 2022. Germany's vice-chancellor confronted him at the table and called his presence irritating.
  408. Sep 1 [moderate] Eight people were arrested over assaults on Palestinians and mosque arsons in the West Bank, days after Israel's prime minister condemned the settler raids at Qusra and Jalud. It is the first reported enforcement action following that condemnation.
  409. Sep 2 [extreme] The United States struck Iranian air-defence installations, radar sites, anti-ship cruise-missile launchers and Jiroft airport in Kerman province around the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian officials reported civilian deaths including at a wedding in Hormozgan; carriers give differing tolls and no American command has published an account.
  410. Sep 2 [critical] Jordan's armed forces said thirteen ballistic missiles entered the Kingdom's airspace, that ten were intercepted and three fell in remote areas, after Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it struck American bases there. Kuwait and Bahrain separately reported Iranian drone attacks with no injuries or damage.
  411. Sep 2 [critical] Two supertankers were struck by projectiles minutes apart near Khasab inside the Strait of Hormuz: the Sidr, run by Saudi Arabia's Bahri, and the Senegal Prosperity, operated by South Korea's Sinokor. No casualties were reported and no party has claimed the attacks.
  412. Sep 2 [critical] Germany formally blamed Russia for the explosive drone found at Leipzig airport in August, saying it had proof the operators worked for Russian state entities, and closed a Russian consulate and a cultural centre. NATO's Secretary-General said the evidence was clear; the EU called it state-sponsored terrorism.
  413. Sep 2 [high] Putin publicly pledged support to Iran at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit, where leaders signed the Bishkek Declaration and the organisation issued a statement condemning military strikes on Iran and unilateral coercive measures.
  414. Sep 2 [critical] A Russian overnight attack killed at least sixteen people and injured fifty-four across Ukraine, with Kyiv and Odesa worst hit, on the seventh consecutive night. Putin separately ordered preparations for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy system and dismissed mobilisation reports.
  415. Sep 2 [high] The American channel with Russia was named: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met Finance Minister Anton Siluanov at the Group of Twenty meeting in Asheville on 31 August to discuss a twenty-eight-point peace plan. A Ukrainian official said Kyiv knew nothing of the meeting; the White House briefings page opened and carries no readout.
  416. Sep 2 [high] No negotiated limit has bound American or Russian strategic nuclear forces since 5 February 2026, when New START expired with no successor. Inspections, data declarations and telemetry exchange all lapsed with it. Russia offered to keep observing the old ceilings for a year; the United States did not respond. It is the first such gap since 1972.
  417. Sep 2 [critical] A United States Central Command spokesman, Tim Hawkins, said the American military never targets civilians and that reports of the wedding deaths at Kuhestak in Hormozgan originated from Iranian state media. It is the first on-the-record American comment on the resumed strikes recorded here; no command has published an account of the strikes themselves. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman called them a catalogue of atrocities, and the Iranian Red Crescent wrote to the International Criminal Court's prosecutor. The Hormozgan governor's office named four dead, including a four-year-old boy, and more than sixty injured; the Red Crescent gave a higher toll.
  418. Sep 2 [critical] Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry said Iran attacked the Bahri supertanker Sidr as it transited the Strait of Hormuz on 1 September, and that two Filipino crew members were killed. Iran's Revolutionary Guard says the tankers struck mines. Kuwait and Qatar condemned the attack. It is the first named attribution and the first reported deaths from the two tanker strikes.
  419. Sep 2 [high] Ukraine's commander-in-chief, Mykhailo Drapatyi, issued leadership guidelines pledging accountability and pushing authority down to combat-tested sergeants. This dashboard had no record that Drapatyi has held the post since 21 July 2026, replacing Oleksandr Syrskyi. The appointment decree itself has not yet been read at a primary.
  420. Sep 2 [moderate] Kpler recorded five, 11 and six vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz on 31 August, 1 and 2 September, a 10-day average of 13 a day, and Lloyd's List Intelligence about 12 transits a day from 26 August to 1 September, against about 100 a day before the war.
  421. Sep 3 [critical] Iran struck Kuwait for the second time in three days and warned Washington that all-out war could return. Kuwait's army said it intercepted an incoming missile and drone attack. No casualties or damage have been reported.
  422. Sep 3 [high] The Financial Times reported that Russian specialists are helping Iran develop supersonic cruise missiles, working on the propulsion system. It is the most direct account yet of Russian material support to the state the United States is bombing.
  423. Sep 3 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry record reopened after four days unread, showing no Chinese military aircraft around the island on 3 September and one the day before. Naval presence held at five vessels with three Chinese government ships alongside.
  424. Sep 3 [high] Russia said it would close Goethe-Institut cultural centres, answering Germany's closure of the Russian House in Berlin and the Russian consulate in Bonn over the Leipzig airport drone.
  425. Sep 3 [moderate] The Treasury's press-release index published a readout of the Treasury secretary's 30 August meeting with the Bank of Japan governor, and carries none for his 31 August meeting with Russia's finance minister. The index is current and carries that kind of item for that official.
  426. Sep 3 [high] Poland's prime minister said a fire at a drone-components plant was deliberate sabotage after a masked figure was recorded entering the site. Prosecutors opened a terrorism investigation. No state has been named.
  427. Sep 3 [high] Ukraine's military intelligence confirmed the strike on the Novatek fuel plant and port complex at Ust-Luga on the Baltic, saying a large fire destroyed key equipment.
  428. Sep 3 [high] A Russian air force general was shot by a gunman on a motorcycle near Saratov. His condition has not been established, no Ukrainian body has claimed the attack, and Ukrainian sources say he ordered a strike on a Kyiv children's hospital.
  429. Sep 3 [high] Two Palestinian teenagers were killed at a West Bank village. Accounts differ on whether settlers or Israeli soldiers fired the fatal shots, and the outlets carrying the story give different names for the dead.
  430. Sep 3 [high] A far-right Israeli minister presented a plan for the removal of the Palestinian population from Gaza, framed as voluntary emigration. It is a ministerial proposal, not government policy, and no cabinet decision has been reported.
  431. Sep 4 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded no Chinese military aircraft around the island for a further day, with five navy vessels and five other Chinese government vessels — two more government vessels than the day before.
  432. Sep 4 [high] South Korea was reported to be preparing a naval logistics ship, maritime patrol aircraft and about 150 personnel for the Strait of Hormuz under American pressure. Seoul's presidential office said the reports differed from the facts and that nothing had been decided, adding only that it was discussing ways to help restore free navigation.
  433. Sep 4 [critical] Houthi forces opened their first major ground offensive in four years on Yemen's west coast, pushing toward the port of Mokha and the heights above the Bab el-Mandeb strait and firing more than twenty-five ballistic missiles at the port. A news-agency tally put the dead at 129 across the opening days: sixty-six government troops, sixty-two Houthi fighters and one civilian.
  434. Sep 4 [high] The United States sanctioned the Turkish bank Golden Global, which the State Department called a financial lifeline moving Iranian oil revenue. The bank threatened legal action. It is the first time in this war that Washington has aimed a designation at a bank in a NATO member state.
  435. Sep 4 [high] The Treasury was reported to have issued general licences allowing BP, Shell, Chevron, Eni and Repsol to operate in Venezuela. It is the first sanctions relief this dashboard's reverse query has surfaced; the same query found nothing lifted for Russia or Iran.
  436. Sep 5 [critical] Ukraine ordered a three-day halt to fighting as American envoys prepared to visit Moscow and Kyiv, and Kyiv's air-raid alert sounded as the pause began. Russia rejected the ceasefire and kept striking: seven people were killed and fifty-one wounded across Ukraine over the past day.
  437. Sep 5 [critical] Hezbollah flew a drone at Israeli troops in southern Lebanon and the Israeli military, which said it shot the drone down without casualties, called the launch a violation of the June truce. It is the first Hezbollah fire against Israeli forces since that truce was struck. Israeli strikes on five locations killed three people and wounded twenty-three, among them two children and six rescue workers.
  438. Sep 6 [moderate] Germans voted in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, where the far-right AfD is projected to win the most seats and could form the first far-right state government in Germany since the war. It is a state election, not a federal one, and no result had been published when this was written.
  439. Sep 6 [high] Yemen's internationally recognised government flew fifteen air strikes of its own against Houthi positions in Taiz and Hodeidah rather than relying on Saudi-led coalition air power, and its forces claimed a district on the road toward Mokha. Saudi Arabia has said nothing at all about the offensive.
  440. Sep 6 [critical] Israeli strikes killed four people and wounded twenty in southern Lebanon after Hezbollah launched two drones at Israeli troops, the second attributed Hezbollah launch in two days. Lebanon's health ministry gave the toll; the Israeli military said both drones were shot down without casualties on its side.
  441. Sep 6 [high] American envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner travelled to Kyiv after more than three hours with Putin in Moscow, their first visit to Ukraine in this process. The White House said the Moscow talks covered next steps for ending the war; neither side published a document, a proposal or a date.
  442. Sep 6 [high] The United Nations humanitarian office said 1,800 families were displaced from Taiz in two days as the Houthi offensive on Yemen's west coast continued. It is the first civilian-displacement figure published for this offensive, against a fighter toll now above three hundred.
