  443. Sep 6 [high] Russia's foreign minister said German accusations over the Leipzig airport drone amount to the start of a real war with Germany. Berlin attributed the drone to Russian state entities on 1 September and is closing Russia's Bonn consulate on 18 September.
  444. Sep 6 [high] Iran's parliament speaker said the period of proportionate responses is over and warned that any further American attack would meet a faster, heavier and more painful reply. It is a stated abandonment of the tit-for-tat framing both sides have used since the exchange began.
  445. Sep 6 [high] Lebanon's health ministry published a cumulative count: 4,358 killed and 12,359 wounded since 2 March, and 8,920 killed since October 2023. The figure this dashboard refused on 7 September, carried only by Chinese state media, was twelve deaths from the ministry's own.
  446. Sep 7 [critical] Iran said it will declare a prohibited zone in waters outside the Strait of Hormuz within days, with vessels entering it to face penalties. The announcement came from Mohsen Rezaei rather than a naval commander, and no coordinates, entry points or start date were published.
  447. Sep 7 [high] The far-right AfD took about 43.8 percent in Saxony-Anhalt against roughly 18 percent for the Christian Democrats, short of a majority. The Christian Democrats, Social Democrats, Greens and Left all refuse to govern with it; the BSW, on about 5.3 percent, has not ruled it out. Poland's foreign minister called the result very worrying and France called it a serious moment.
  448. Sep 7 [high] Russia and North Korea opened the first road bridge across their shared border, adding a road link to the single rail crossing that has carried their wartime trade.
  449. Sep 7 [high] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 21 Chinese military aircraft and 13 median-line crossings in the twenty-four hours to 6 September, alongside ten navy vessels and five other government ships. The count fell back to two aircraft the next day while navy vessels rose to thirteen. This dashboard had refused the same surge a day earlier because it reached it through an outlet outside its source directory.
  450. Sep 7 [critical] Israeli strikes killed eleven people in southern Lebanon overnight, including two infants, at Kfar Reman and Deir Zahrani. The Israeli army had ordered the area evacuated before the strikes. It is a separate incident from the four killed on 6 September at Arab Salim, and roughly triples the toll.
  451. Sep 7 [moderate] The Treasury's sanctions page carries a Russia-related designation removal dated 3 September. It is the first positive result this dashboard's reverse query — the standing check for sanctions being lifted rather than imposed — has returned since the check was added.
  452. Sep 7 [high] Qatar is building a legal case for compensation from Iran over missile and drone attacks since 28 February, including strikes on Ras Laffan and Mesaieed, citing an estimated $26bn in infrastructure damage and up to $20bn a year in lost gas revenue, and invoking Security Council Resolution 2817. No forum or amount has been filed.
  453. Sep 7 [high] Ukraine's intelligence chief said units of Russia's 101st Missile Brigade, equipped with the nuclear-capable Oreshnik, are deployed in Belarus — which Zelensky said in February had drawn Belarus into the war — and that Minsk is allowing radio repeaters that help adjust Russian Shahed strikes on Ukraine. Kyiv assesses the direct threat from Belarus as low and sees no sign Minsk is preparing to enter the war.
  454. Sep 7 [high] Shipping documents traced 46 tonnes of a carbon-fibre precursor from China's Jilin Chemical Fiber Group to Alabuga-Volokno, a Rosatom subsidiary that builds attack drones — enough for about 1,300 drones by one expert estimate. The documents, gathered by a Kyiv research centre, were judged legitimate by a US congressional committee; China's embassy called it an attempt to smear and scapegoat China.
  455. Sep 8 [critical] Russia resumed strikes on Kyiv after the three-day pause on capitals, killing two people and injuring sixteen. Ukraine counted 32 cruise missiles, 166 drones and at least twelve ballistic missiles across the night.
  456. Sep 8 [critical] The nuclear agency told its board that inspectors have been unable to carry out on-site verification in Iran, and that more than a year has passed since it lost continuity of knowledge over uranium enriched to 60 percent. France, Germany, the United Kingdom and the United States are drafting a resolution referring the file to the Security Council — the first such referral in two decades.
  457. Sep 8 [high] Canada's counter-tariffs on about $20bn of United States goods took effect at one minute past midnight, covering more than seven hundred products at rates from 15 to 50 percent. Trump threatened to block Bombardier aircraft sales in the United States.
  458. Sep 8 [critical] Houthi ballistic missiles and drones struck energy-sector facilities in four southern Saudi provinces — Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jizan and Najran — wounding 73 civilians and forcing a temporary halt to some operations, Saudi officials said. The Houthi military spokesman called it a large-scale, long-range operation.
  459. Sep 8 [high] Britain said it would ban trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, drawing public criticism from the United States ambassador, from Israel and from some British MPs.
  460. Sep 8 [critical] A Russian drone crossed Moldovan and Romanian airspace and crashed inside Moldova, and NATO jets were scrambled. A separate Russian drone strike killed two people at a crossing on the Ukraine-Moldova border. Moldova's president said Russia's front line is moving west.
  461. Sep 8 [high] Twelve countries joined Britain's settlement-trade measures — Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden among those named — after Israel published tenders for about 1,200 homes in the E1 area.
  462. Sep 8 [critical] Trump spoke with Putin by telephone after his envoys' visits to Moscow and Kyiv, the Kremlin said: Putin set out his vision of a peace process and assured Trump that Russia has no aggressive plans toward Europe, and Trump said ending the war would open the door to restoring relations. No breakthrough; Washington is pushing for trilateral talks and Zelensky hopes to meet Trump around 20 September.
  463. Sep 8 [high] Hungary expelled ten staff of Russia's diplomatic mission for activities its foreign minister called unacceptable under the Vienna Convention, two weeks after Budapest designated Russia a threat to Europe. Russia's foreign ministry promised a harsh and painful response.
  464. Sep 8 [critical] Britain imposed an import ban on settlement goods, sanctions on those expanding settlements and a refusal of arms-export licences supporting the occupation, its foreign secretary saying settler terrorism is rampant; twelve countries including France and Canada joined. Israel ordered Britain's Jerusalem consulate closed, expelled British representatives from the Gaza support centre and the Ramallah training team, and barred twelve British nationals.
  465. Sep 9 [high] Ukrainian drones struck the naval base and an oil-shipping terminal at Novorossiysk, Ukraine's General Staff said, with the president citing hits on cruise-missile carriers. The local authority said only that debris had fallen.
  466. Sep 9 [high] Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar and Egypt condemned Iran's ballistic-missile attack on Jordan. It is the first time in this war that the Gulf mediators have criticised Tehran by name over a strike on a partner state's territory.
  467. Sep 9 [critical] Russian strikes killed at least twelve people and injured seventy-two across Ukraine, including six railway workers, as attacks on Kyiv continued for a second night after the pause on capitals ended.
  468. Sep 9 [high] Israel ordered Britain to close its East Jerusalem consulate within thirty days and gave British staff at the American-led Gaza coordination mission seven days to leave.
  469. Sep 9 [high] The United States will ban imports of most Canadian alcohol, some dairy goods and motorcycles from 29 September, a day after Canada's counter-tariffs on about $20bn of American goods took effect.
  470. Sep 9 [high] Brent crude closed at $101.21 a barrel on 9 September after the United States destroyed five Iranian tankers and Iran struck a base in Jordan, having traded as high as $101.71. This dashboard earlier reported no close above $100 from a mid-session reading.
  471. Sep 9 [high] Saudi Arabia was reported striking back in Yemen a day after Houthi missiles hit its southern energy sites. The corroborating detail available describes Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces at Marib and on the west coast, not confirmed Saudi air strikes. No named operation was announced.
  472. Sep 9 [critical] The nuclear agency told its board that North Korea has built a new uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon, with capacity described as about 28 centrifuge cascades, and said it violates Security Council resolutions. Construction began in 2024 and the exterior was complete by mid-2025.
  473. Sep 9 [critical] The nuclear agency's board voted to refer Iran to the United Nations Security Council for breaching its non-proliferation obligations — twenty-three in favour, Russia, China and Niger against, eight abstentions. Britain, France, Germany and the United States submitted the resolution. It is the first such referral in twenty years, and Russia and China can veto any sanctions that follow.
  474. Sep 9 [critical] The Revolutionary Guard claimed strikes on two US vessels, eight oil tankers and ten other ships in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman, and said its prohibited zone now covers parts of the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. It named no vessel and gave no coordinates; UKMTO said several vessels in the Gulf of Oman and the Gulf were subject to disabling fire, without saying who fired.
  475. Sep 9 [high] Pakistan's defence minister said aggression against one member of the Mecca defence pact is aggression against all three, and that an attack spilling into Saudi Arabia would make it operational.   476. Sep 9 [high] Trump said the Iran war would not end until after the November midterm elections and, at his party's convention, warned Iran "not to get cute" over activity at the Pickaxe Mountain site, saying the United States would hit it very hard.
  477. Sep 9 [high] Ukrainian drones struck a gas facility in Russia's Yamalo-Nenets region, more than 3,000 km from the border, Ukraine's General Staff said — the deepest strike of the war. Fires were separately reported in Dagestan after a drone attack on a Caspian port.
  478. Sep 10 [high] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded eighteen Chinese military aircraft in the day to 10 September, thirteen of them crossing the median line, with eight navy vessels and one other government ship. The daily aircraft count has run 21, 2, 8, 6 and now 18.
  479. Sep 10 [critical] The Houthis seized the Red Sea port city of Mokha, near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, after days of fighting with Saudi-backed government forces. Yemeni government military sources confirmed the loss to Reuters, government forces and their allies relocated south to Dhubab, and presidential council head Rashad al-Alimi said developments around the port are not a purely Yemeni affair. The UN Security Council met in emergency session the same day.
  480. Sep 10 [high] A US official told Reuters that Iran's missile attack this week on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan damaged American military aircraft: one A-10 attack jet was left with a missing wing, and about eight F-15s were lightly damaged and returned to service. US forces fired roughly thirty Patriot interceptors. The official was not named.
  481. Sep 10 [high] Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman twice asked Trump by phone for US strikes on the Houthis, and Trump declined, Axios reported, citing US officials who said Washington would keep its focus on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters said it could not verify the report.
  482. Sep 11 [critical] Houthi forces seized Perim island, also called Mayyun, in the Bab el-Mandeb strait on 11 September, a day after taking the port city of Mokha, and two Yemeni government sources told Reuters they had also reached the town of Dhubab.   483. Sep 11 [high] Vladimir Putin arrived in New Delhi for a two-day BRICS summit hosted by India, expected to be dominated by the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian is attending, and China's Xi Jinping is expected.
  484. Sep 11 [critical] Saudi Arabia shut its East-West oil pipeline as a precaution after its foreign ministry said drones launched from Iraqi territory hit it in the Riyadh and Medina areas, causing injuries and damage. Riyadh said it would hold off on retaliating to give Baghdad an opportunity to act; Iraq's prime minister dismissed a military commander and ordered an investigation, and two Iraqi sources told Reuters the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran was closed.
  485. Sep 11 [critical] Houthi forces took the Hanish islands on 10 September alongside Mokha, then Perim island and Dhubab on 11 September. A Yemeni government military official told AFP they now hold Yemen's entire Red Sea coast, and government sources told Reuters the group has near control of the Bab el-Mandeb.
  486. Sep 13 [high] A Russian drone struck the locomotive of a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train about 2 km from the Polish border, shortly after a train carrying Boris Johnson, David Petraeus and Carl Bildt passed through. No one was hurt, and Poland issued air-raid alerts for border counties; nothing was reported entering Polish territory.
  487. Sep 13 [high] Trump said Zelensky "has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia", blaming Ukraine's strikes for a global diesel shortage; hours earlier Ukraine's military said it had hit the TANECO refinery in Russia's Tatarstan republic.
  488. Sep 13 [high] Oman postponed the meeting of Gulf states and Iran on the Strait of Hormuz planned for Salalah on 14 September, giving no new date. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said Saudi Arabia asked for the delay, citing events in Yemen; Oman said the aim was conditions for constructive dialogue.
  489. Sep 13 [high] US officials held direct talks with Houthi representatives at the US embassy in Muscat over the weekend of 12-13 September, with Omani help, Reuters reported citing three sources. The Houthis said they had no intention of attacking US vessels and remained committed to their 2025 ceasefire with Washington.
  490. Sep 14 [moderate] The EU extended by a week, to midnight on 22 September, its deadline to renew sanctions on about 2,600 Russian individuals and entities, as France and Slovakia push to delist oligarch Alisher Usmanov; Zelensky said it is "definitely not the time to shield Russian oligarchs from sanctions".
  491. Sep 14 [high] Trump posted that "Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy Targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!"; Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to halt its strikes only if partners ensure Russia stops hitting Ukraine's electricity, and neither Kyiv nor Moscow confirmed a deal.
  492. Sep 14 [high] The United States sanctioned VTB Bank, one of Russia's largest banks, for helping Iran evade sanctions, under an order targeting Iran's financial sector; the Treasury warned foreign banks still dealing with VTB of greater sanctions risk.
  493. Sep 14 [high] The Pentagon's inspector general told Congress that munitions use in the Iran war has caused "strategic inventory shortfalls" and exposed industrial bottlenecks, putting the operation's cost at $33.4 billion to 30 June, $22.3 billion of it munitions, and listing four F-15s and up to 30 Reaper drones destroyed. It also said Iranian strikes damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings at US bases in eight countries and listed 18 US military dead as of 27 August.
  494. Sep 14 [high] US Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said the United States now has on-orbit "space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action"; China's foreign ministry and the Kremlin objected.
  495. Sep 14 [high] UN-appointed investigators said there are reasonable grounds to believe US strikes on a school in Minab (more than 150 killed, about 120 of them children) and in Lamerd (22 civilians) on 28 February were war crimes; US Central Command has said it did not strike Lamerd that day. The same mission found that killings of protesters by Iran's security forces occurred on a massive scale.
  496. Sep 15 [high] NATO fighter jets shot down a drone that flew into Lithuania from Belarus overnight into 15 September. Lithuania's defence minister, Robertas Kaunas, said an explosive device was found at the crash site near Kruonis and neutralised; Italy, whose jets downed it, said it most probably came from Russia.
  497. Sep 15 [high] The Saudi-led coalition said Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif wounded 13 civilians and damaged seven homes and two vehicles; its spokesman said the coalition would respond "responsibly and firmly".
  498. Sep 15 [high] Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck Russia's Syzran oil refinery and the Atlant Aero drone plant in Taganrog overnight, a day after Trump said both sides had agreed to stop hitting energy targets; Samara's governor said more than 40 drones were shot down over the region.
  499. Sep 15 [high] Saudi Arabia said its air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone heading for Mecca on Tuesday evening, before it entered restricted airspace; coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki called the security of the holy mosques and pilgrims a "red line". The Houthis denied targeting Mecca, and later claimed they shot down a Saudi F-15 over Marib, which has not been independently confirmed. The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation and the Arab League chief condemned the attempt.
  500. Sep 15 [high] The US Justice Department charged five alleged agents of Russian intelligence, including former intelligence colonel Yuri Khrameev and his son, over a network it says tried this summer to have a Russian dissident in the US murdered and planned attacks on infrastructure in European countries backing Ukraine. All five remain at large.
  501. Sep 15 [high] Reuters reported that three of Russia's six largest diesel refineries have halted or cut output in September after Ukrainian drone strikes: Kirishi has shut down, and NORSI and Volgograd are running at about a quarter of capacity. Leningrad region's governor introduced temporary fuel limits at filling stations until 1 October.
  502. Sep 16 [high] The US House passed the Russia sanctions bill named for the late Senator Lindsey Graham by 262 votes to 159 on 16 September, with 58 Democrats joining most Republicans, sending it to President Trump after the Senate's 86-11 vote in August. It would sanction Russian officials, companies and banks and let the president impose tariffs of up to 100% on major importers of Russian oil and gas, such as China and India.
  503. Sep 16 [moderate] Trump threatened the EU over its offer to make Canada its first associate member: "If I think it's at all a hostile act, I will put very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe on many things," he told reporters, calling the proposal "laughable". France's Europe minister said the United States has no veto over European choices.
  504. Sep 17 [high] Saudi Arabia has asked France, Pakistan, Egypt and the United Kingdom to deploy air-defence support as it runs low on missile interceptors, two officials told the Associated Press. Reuters reported that President Trump has so far rebuffed Saudi pleas for US military support against the Houthis.
  505. Sep 17 [high] Wreckage from a Houthi drone shot down over Taif killed a Yemeni resident and injured two people, one critically, Saudi civil defence said — the first reported death in Saudi Arabia in the current escalation. Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, the Arab League and the EU condemned the attack.
  506. Sep 17 [moderate] The US State Department approved a possible $24.3 billion sale to Saudi Arabia of 48 F-35 fighter jets with engines and support equipment; the sale still requires congressional approval. Saudi Arabia's embassy welcomed it as a sign of the strategic partnership.
  507. Sep 17 [moderate] Slovakia's Prime Minister Robert Fico said he does not want Slovakia to be part of an armed conflict "because of some Article 5", NATO's mutual-defence clause, while saying Slovakia values its membership; he called the Russia-Ukraine war "out of control".
  508. Sep 18 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 28 Chinese military aircraft around the island in the day to 18 September, 24 of them crossing the median line, with 7 navy vessels and 2 official ships — the fourth daily rise in a row, from 4 aircraft on 14 September.
  509. Sep 18 [high] The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said on 18 September that a tanker had been hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire that was put out; the crew were reported safe.   510. Sep 18 [moderate] South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung said three times that Seoul will not send troops to the Strait of Hormuz, despite growing US pressure: "There will be no engagement or involvement in war." He said South Korea would carry out only the minimum activity needed to protect its own ships.
  511. Sep 18 [high] President Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law on 18 September. It lets the president impose tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and natural gas, sanctions Putin, Russian officials, oligarchs and banks, and extends US sanctions on Iran's energy and weapons sectors. China and India, the largest buyers of Russian crude, are most exposed.
  512. Sep 18 [moderate] The US, Denmark and Greenland announced a defence pact covering US military bases, troops and security operations in Greenland, to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week subject to approval by the Danish and Greenlandic parliaments.   513. Sep 19 [high] Saudi civil defence issued its first air-raid alerts for Riyadh since the Houthi war escalated, and for al-Kharj and other regions, overnight on 18-19 September; AFP and Reuters journalists heard two explosions before an all-clear about half an hour later. Saudi Arabia has not said where the threat came from.
  514. Sep 19 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 20 Chinese military aircraft around the island in the day to 19 September, 13 of them crossing the median line, with 11 navy vessels — the highest naval count this month — and 3 official ships.
  515. Sep 19 [critical] Saudi-led coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki said air defences intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile fired at Riyadh at dawn on 19 September, and that Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu were also targeted. Saudi authorities reported no casualties or damage in Riyadh. This attributes the capital's first air-raid alerts, which were unsourced at the morning update.
  516. Sep 20 [critical] Ukraine attacked the Moscow region with hundreds of drones on the final day of Russia's parliamentary election, killing at least two people; Russian officials said the Moscow Oil Refinery at Kapotnya and a logistics park at Sofyino were struck and that drones reached 16 regions.   517. Sep 20 [high] The European Union's listings on roughly 2,600 Russians are running on a seven-day technical extension that expires on 22 September, after member states failed to agree a six-month renewal. France and Slovakia are withholding agreement to secure the removal of Alisher Usmanov, and unanimity is required.
  518. Sep 20 [high] Iran's central military command said it had information that the United States is preparing to resume strikes and warned that states allowing US use of their territory would be considered complicit. Trump told Fox News he is in a 'deciding mode', weighing military action, economic pressure or a deal, and said he would be open to meeting Iran's president at the UN.
  519. Sep 20 [high] Iranian lawmakers submitted a bill with triple urgency to withdraw Iran from the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty; it needs the parliament speaker's approval to reach the floor.   520. Sep 20 [high] Xi Jinping will meet President Trump at the White House on Thursday 24 September, the first state visit by a Chinese leader in eleven years. Treasury Secretary Bessent and trade representative Greer met Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York on 20 September ahead of the visit, on the trade truce, rare earths and AI.
  521. Sep 20 [moderate] Taiwan's defence ministry recorded 5 Chinese military aircraft, all crossing the median line, 11 navy ships and 6 other government ships in the day to 20 September — the month's highest count of government ships. This dashboard earlier said no 20 September record had been published; that was wrong.
  522. Sep 22 [high] EU governments renewed sanctions listings on about 2,600 Russian individuals and entities for three years — the first renewal beyond six months — after agreeing to remove billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman. Latvia abstained; Ukraine opposed the removals.
  523. Sep 24 [critical] Iran proposed a seven-day plan to end the war, presented by Foreign Minister Araghchi to US envoy Steve Witkoff at the UN: a halt on all fronts including Lebanon, frozen assets released, oil sanctions lifted and the US blockade ended, with the Strait of Hormuz reopening on day seven.
  524. Sep 24 [critical] The Saudi-led coalition said air defences intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Taif and the Yanbu oil port; a Greek air-defence crew at Yanbu downed a missile and a drone. Mecca received its first civil-defence alert in about a decade. No damage was reported.
  525. Sep 24 [high] Xi Jinping's two-day state visit to Washington ended with the US-China trade truce extended by two months to 10 January, a commitment to explore a channel for AI security incidents, and no deals on tariffs, rare earths, chips or Taiwan.
  526. Sep 25 [high] Russia launched 282 drones plus Zircon and ballistic missiles at Ukraine overnight into 25 September; seven people were killed in Kyiv, including a 14-year-old, and 59 injured, with strikes continuing into the day.
  527. Sep 26 [critical] Trump rejected Iran's seven-day plan to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, calling it not acceptable. No US counter-proposal was published and no strike followed.
  528. Sep 27 [high] British counter-terrorism police arrested five men near RAF Fairford, a base US bombers use in the Iran war, on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act; police say those held are UK nationals from London. Iran denied any link.
  529. Sep 27 [high] Russian drones and a missile struck Kyiv for a fourth straight night, killing two and injuring at least eight at a market and a gas station. On 28 September daytime drone strikes hit the National Academy of Sciences and a medical centre in central Kyiv.
  530. Sep 27 [high] Trump said Ukraine should take it easy on Russian refineries; a Ukrainian official told the Kyiv Independent that Kyiv would stop only if Russia agrees to an energy truce, and nothing has been agreed.
  531. Sep 28 [high] Brent's expiring November contract rose more than 3% to about $107 a barrel after Trump's rejection of Iran's plan; December, now the front month, traded near $100.   532. Sep 28 [high] The US and China released reciprocal lists of about $30bn of goods each on which they will cut tariffs, from consumer electronics to farm products; no strategic goods are included.
  533. Sep 29 [high] The Saudi-led coalition said a Houthi attack at 05:11 on 29 September disabled a transformer at Medina's Taibah power station, which supplies the Prophet's Mosque; the Houthis denied it. Turkey, Qatar, the Arab League and Al-Azhar condemned the strike.
  534. Sep 30 [critical] Russia attacked Kyiv from overnight into the evening of 30 September, with 285 drones in the daytime phase alone, 254 of them intercepted, after an overnight wave of drones and Zircon, Oniks and Iskander missiles across Ukraine.   535. Sep 30 [moderate] The Pentagon said the last US troops had left Iraq, departing Erbil airbase as the coalition mission against the Islamic State ended on 30 September; operations moved to Jordan, and hundreds of US troops remain in Syria.
  536. Oct 1 [high] The US Treasury designated Russia's A7 shadow-banking network, its sub-agents and the rouble-backed A7A5 token as a transnational criminal organisation, saying the network moved $140 million from Iranian sanctions-evasion entities. Separately it sanctioned Iran's carmakers, state railway and steel exporters.
  537. Oct 1 [critical] Putin told the Valdai forum that an attack on Kaliningrad would put the use of "all weapons" in Russia's arsenal on the agenda, a day after Russian embassies said Russia would use nuclear weapons if NATO tried to isolate the exclave. NATO denounced the "irresponsible nuclear rhetoric."
  538. Oct 1 [high] British police arrested a 27-year-old British-Iranian dual national in London on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts in the RAF Fairford investigation; the five men first arrested were released on bail without charge. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were "strong indications that Iran played a part"; Iran denied involvement and summoned Britain's ambassador.
  539. Oct 1 [high] The US urged European allies to release strategic diesel reserves immediately as Trump said he was thinking about banning US diesel exports; the EU's trade chief warned a ban would have very dramatic consequences. US diesel averages $6.39 a gallon, up more than 70% since the war began.
  540. Oct 2 [high] The US is sending a third aircraft carrier, the Theodore Roosevelt, and about 2,000 Marines toward Iran, a US official told Al Jazeera, with the full buildup due by the end of November. Trump said Iran would be "hit very hard" but has signalled no action before the midterms.
  541. Oct 2 [high] A 2.5-million-barrel supertanker caught fire after being hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, according to UKMTO as reported by Al Jazeera; the ship has not been named.
  542. Oct 2 [high] G7 governments agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency oil and diesel stocks over four months, coordinated by the International Energy Agency, with a large diesel release in the first 20 days. Trump then said the US would not ban diesel exports, and Brent briefly fell below $100 before rebounding to about $102 by evening.
  543. Oct 4 [high] The Pentagon said all US bombers deployed to RAF Fairford have returned to their home bases in the United States over security concerns after the alleged plot against the base; about a dozen B-1s had been stationed there, Al Jazeera reported. Prime Minister Burnham suggested last week that Iran played a part; Iran denies it.
  544. Oct 4 [high] A projectile struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on 4 October, damaging its engine room, UKMTO said; the crew is reported safe and the attacker is unidentified. It is the latest in a run of attacks on tankers in the Strait since the supertanker fire on 2 October.
  545. Oct 4 [high] Yemen's Saudi-backed government launched an offensive to retake all Houthi-held territory after the Houthis took Turbah, a town on the main Aden–Taiz road; the Saudi-led coalition said it carried out 97 strikes on Houthi forces, and air strikes hit Sanaa and Saada.
  546. Oct 5 [high] Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan activated their Mecca defence pact for the first time, agreeing at an emergency Riyadh meeting to 'provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment' to Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks, under each country's laws. No force size was given.
  547. Oct 7 [critical] Houthi missile and drone attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport on 6 and 7 October killed three civilians and injured 36, Saudi civil aviation authorities said. The Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on the Riyadh airport, and explosions were heard in Riyadh on 8 October.
  548. Oct 7 [high] A tanker was hit by multiple projectiles about 94 km north of Madinat ash Shamal off Qatar's north coast, with casualties reported, UKMTO said; it is the first reported tanker attack in the western Gulf in weeks, and no attacker was named.
  549. Oct 7 [critical] Russia launched 48 cruise missiles, ballistic missiles and 130 drones at Ukraine overnight into 7 October, Putin's birthday, Ukraine's Air Force said. At least 30 people were killed, more than 20 of them in Pryluky, including five children.
  550. Oct 7 [high] Denmark's intelligence service said Russia has moved from planning to attempting sabotage against Danish firms supplying Ukraine, targeting weapons production, Reuters reports; it named no firms, and Russia's embassy denied it.
  551. Oct 9 [critical] Trump said he agreed with Putin to let Russian diesel onto world markets, starting with more than 300,000 tonnes, and the Treasury issued a Russia-related general licence on 9 October; Euromaidan Press reports it authorises Russian diesel sales until April 2027. Russia said it partially lifted its diesel export ban the next day.
  552. Oct 9 [high] The US Treasury placed the International Criminal Court itself on its sanctions list, with a six-month grace period; Britain, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Denmark, Canada and Japan said they 'regret and strongly disagree' with the move.
  553. Oct 10 [critical] A missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on 10 October killed 12 people and wounded 309, Saudi authorities said; France 24 called it the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade. No group has claimed it; the Saudi-led coalition blamed the Houthis and vowed a 'decisive response'.
  554. Oct 10 [critical] Trump said Ukraine should 'get a new president' and that Zelensky 'better damn well stop' striking Russian refineries. Zelensky called the diesel deal a 'weak decision'; EU foreign policy chief Kallas said it was 'not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't.'
  555. Oct 11 [high] Trump announced an 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine, saying both had agreed; Kyiv said it was not told in advance, and Moscow has not formally confirmed it. Russia struck Kharkiv's CHP-5 power plant hours later.
  556. Oct 12 [high] EU foreign ministers adopted the bloc's largest-ever set of Russia sanctions listings in Luxembourg on 12 October: 1,569 targets, 826 defence-industry companies and 743 of their executives, with asset freezes and entry bans. Kallas said it was not the time to ease pressure on Moscow.
  557. Oct 12 [high] UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham told Parliament it was 'highly likely' the RAF Fairford incident was coordinated in Iran and 'almost certainly directed' by the Revolutionary Guard; Iran rejected the claim. No one has been charged.
  558. Oct 12 [moderate] EU foreign policy chief Kallas said in a post on X that EU foreign ministers had 'just adopted nearly 1,600 new sanctions listings targeting Russia's military-industrial complex', Tasnim reports.
  559. Oct 12 [high] Ethiopian federal forces had taken Shire, Adigrat, Adwa and Zalambessa up to the Eritrean border before pausing on 12 October, Critical Threats reports.
  560. Oct 13 [critical] Russia fired 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 drones at Ukraine overnight into 14 October, Zelensky said, hitting all three of Kyiv's combined heat and power plants; four people were killed, 25 injured and 600,000 left without power. Kyiv says allies gave no launch warning on 12 or 13 October.
  561. Oct 13 [high] The Houthis hit an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran on 13 October, causing a fire but no casualties, a Saudi energy ministry official said; debris from missiles intercepted over Riyadh injured four people and damaged 15 homes.
  562. Oct 13 [high] The Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride sank in the Strait of Hormuz after being hit and catching fire; all 21 crew were evacuated, Singapore's maritime authority said. Reuters reports it is the war's second ship sinking; the bulk carrier Cape Dao, struck on 23 September, also sank.
  563. Oct 13 [moderate] MI5 chief Ken McCallum called Russia 'aggressor number one', saying it is escalating hybrid attacks below NATO's Article 5 threshold and hiring criminals after nearly 1,000 expulsions of its officers; he cited more than 50 Iran-linked arrests in Britain in a year.
  564. Oct 14 [high] North Korea test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles off its east coast, from a vertical tube and a torpedo tube, South Korea's military said; Stars and Stripes says it is the first publicly reported such test since January 2024.
  565. Oct 15 [high] Russia launched 580 drones and two Kh-59 missiles overnight into 15 October, Ukraine's Air Force said, downing or jamming 536. Kirovohrad's governor called it the oblast's heaviest attack of the war.
  566. Oct 15 [high] Two tankers caught fire off Romania's Sulina, near the Danube mouth, amid drone attacks on Black Sea shipping; seven crew of a San Marino-flagged chemical tanker are missing. Bulgaria said it had no proof Russia was responsible.
  567. Oct 15 [high] Houthi missiles struck Aden's Maashiq presidential palace, the seat of Yemen's government; the cabinet was unharmed. Officials gave tolls ranging from two to five killed.
  568. Oct 16 [critical] Trump signed an executive order implementing Congress's Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act and, in the same order, waived its sanctions and tariffs on Russia with no end date. Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it 'historic'.
  569. Oct 16 [high] Reuters reports, citing two US officials and a Western official, that the order to slow SpaceX's Starshield service for Ukraine's military came from inside the White House. A senior US official said the president made no such request.
  570. Oct 17 [high] Two Romanian F-16s shot down two jet-powered Geran drones over Romanian territorial waters near Sulina on the evening of 17 October, Romania's defence ministry said. NATO's North Atlantic Council holds a special Black Sea session on 20 October at Romania's request.
  571. Oct 18 [high] Taiwan's coast guard drove away 16 Chinese vessels, four of them fishing boats, operating simultaneously around the main island and Pratas, calling it 'hybrid warfare' and an attempt to 'unilaterally alter the status quo'; some entered restricted waters.
  572. Oct 19 [high] Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles and more than 200 drones overnight into 19 October, hitting 28 substations and other energy facilities in 11 oblasts; at least 550,000 households lost power. Zelensky said Ukraine 'once again' had no advance warning from partners.
  573. Oct 19 [high] Zelensky said the Pentagon is delaying missiles European countries have already paid for, pending Defence Secretary Hegseth's signature. Secretary of State Rubio denied intelligence sharing had been withdrawn; Trump said Zelensky 'doesn't know what he's talking about' and that it is time for somebody else to negotiate for Ukraine.
  574. Oct 19 [high] Houthi ballistic missiles struck the al-Alam military camp near Ataq in Shabwa province, where new recruits were training; a Yemeni military source told DPA more than 30 soldiers were killed. The government's army spokesman blamed the Houthis, who have not commented.
  575. Oct 19 [moderate] Kim Yo Jong said North Korea's military is considering deploying 'tactical strike means' along the DMZ, calling the border 'very unstable' after South Korean warning shots at troops crossing the demarcation line; Seoul vowed to retaliate firmly against provocations.
  576. Oct 19 [high] Russia's Cosmos 2612 satellite manoeuvred to within about 500 metres of an ICEYE commercial radar satellite that supports Ukraine between 15 and 19 October, commercial trackers say; LeoLabs called it the most advanced and potentially dangerous uncooperative approach it has observed.
  577. Oct 20 [high] Britain will fly RAF Typhoon jets on 'defensive counter air missions' to protect Saudi cities and infrastructure from Houthi missiles and drones, and extend air-to-air refuelling, the Ministry of Defence said; the jets will not attack the Houthis.
  578. Oct 20 [moderate] China's Southern Theater Command said the USS Charleston 'illegally intruded' near Sabina Shoal in the Spratlys and that its navy tracked the ship; the Philippines said no nation can require permission for lawful transit. Reuters notes the last known US freedom-of-navigation operation there was over a year ago.
  579. Oct 20 [moderate] NATO will send more maritime patrol aircraft, radars, drones and intelligence staff to the Black Sea after drone attacks on shipping, the alliance said after its council met at Romania's request. It announced no new command or naval mission.
  580. Oct 20 [moderate] France and Britain held their first joint airborne nuclear-strike exercise on 20–21 October: RAF Typhoons escorted French Rafales on a simulated nuclear mission over the Mediterranean, France's armed forces ministry said. No nuclear weapons were involved.
  581. Oct 21 [high] US envoy Witkoff met Putin in St Petersburg; the Kremlin says Putin agreed to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the US, possibly next month. Putin said Russia wants talks on a final deal, not a short ceasefire, and freed Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old American.
  582. Oct 21 [high] A late-night attack on Dammam airport killed two people, a Saudi and an Indian, and injured eight, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said; it did not say who carried it out. Arab News reports debris from an intercepted drone killed two workers at the Shaybah oil field the same day.
  583. Oct 21 [moderate] Germany's armed forces raised their Russian sabotage threat level to 'significant', the second-highest, for the first time, Süddeutsche Zeitung reports and a defence ministry spokesperson confirmed. SZ says the trigger was an explosive-laden drone found near Wunstorf air base.
  584. Oct 22 [high] Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed seven tankers were struck on 21–22 October near Hormuz, naming none; AP could not confirm and UKMTO has not reported them. Trump said Iran is 'making up fake hits'. Lloyd's List counts 28 ship attacks in October, the war's highest month.
  585. Oct 22 [high] Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv in three waves overnight into 22 October, plus about 200 drones, Zelensky and the Air Force said; Kyiv's metro was cut in two. At least seven people were killed across Ukraine.
  586. Oct 23 [high] A drone strike sank the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv about 13 nautical miles off Constanta, just outside Romania's territorial waters; one sailor was killed and three are missing. Romania's President Dan called it part of Russia's escalation.
  587. Oct 23 [moderate] Austria expelled four Russian diplomats, three from the embassy and one from Russia's OSCE delegation, for activities incompatible with their status; Moscow said a response is unavoidable.
  588. Oct 23 [moderate] A Russian Geran drone crashed in Moldova's Telenești district, under 100 metres from a home and near an energy facility, the defence ministry said; Moldova expelled a Russian embassy staffer.
  589. Oct 23 [moderate] A Russian diesel cargo for the US under Washington's waiver, about 40,000 tonnes on the tanker Agioi Fanendes, loaded at Primorsk bound for New York and is due on 7 November, Reuters shipping data show; Reuters calls it the first under the Trump–Putin deal.
  590. Oct 23 [moderate] Gunmen attacked a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Jordan's Karak governorate, killing eight and injuring about 40, the health ministry said; three wounded suspects were arrested on 26 October after a firefight. No group has been named.
  591. Oct 23 [moderate] Two Israeli soldiers were killed at a checkpoint near Hebron and both attackers were shot dead; Israel then removed about 250 Palestinian families from the city, its mayor said, and will close West Bank crossings on election day.
  592. Oct 23 [moderate] Drone strikes killed at least 306 people in Sudan in the first three weeks of October, the UN human rights office said, attributing them to both the army and the RSF.
  593. Oct 24 [moderate] Russia and Ukraine agreed a ceasefire in occupied Oleshky from 04:00 on 27 October to let aid in and civilians out; the White House said Melania Trump brokered it, and both militaries confirmed they would observe it.
  594. Oct 24 [moderate] Kim Jong-un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge into China and met Communist Party standing committee member Wang Huning in Dandong, his first China visit since September 2025, Xinhua and Seoul's unification ministry said.
  595. Oct 24 [low] Secretary of State Rubio urged Cubans seeking change to form a 'discrete partnership' with the CIA, a day after Trump said he would deal with Cuba once Iran is settled.
  596. Oct 24 [moderate] Iran's armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi said Iran 'will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances', state television reported; Trump said on 23 October, 'We may do another little Epic Fury.'
  597. Oct 25 [moderate] Kremlin aide Ushakov said Russia will be ready to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the US after 4 November; Zelensky says technical meetings are planned in the first half of November, possibly in Abu Dhabi. No date is set.
  598. Oct 25 [moderate] Kremlin aide Ushakov said Moscow, Beijing and Washington are 'in principle ready' for a Putin–Trump–Xi meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18–19 November; neither Washington nor Beijing has confirmed it.
  599. Oct 25 [moderate] Lula won Brazil's presidential runoff with just over 51 percent to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48 percent at 98.76 percent counted; Bolsonaro said it is 'impossible to recognise the results' and pledged to annul the vote.
  600. Oct 25 [moderate] Serbia's President Vučić conceded his party lost the snap parliamentary election to the student-led movement; a CESID projection gives the Student List 138 of 250 seats on turnout near 70 percent.
  601. Oct 25 [moderate] CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper flew over the Strait of Hormuz and said its primary transit routes remain free of Iranian sea mines; CENTCOM says US support helped Gulf states export more than 1.5 billion barrels since the summer.
  602. Oct 25 [moderate] The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh as the capital's airport partly reopened, and that it destroyed two missile launchers in Sanaa; no casualties were reported.
  603. Oct 25 [low] Israel's Channel 12 reported that army chief Eyal Zamir resisted a Netanyahu order for military action tied to Iran; Netanyahu called the report nonsense and Defence Minister Katz called talk of a rift baseless.
  604. Oct 26 [moderate] Saudi Arabia's defence minister, Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir and Turkey's intelligence chief are due in Tehran for security talks between the Mecca pact states and Iran, Iranian state media say; Iran told Munir there will be no US talks until its demands are met.
  605. Oct 26 [moderate] Saudi Arabia's defence minister Khalid bin Salman, Turkey's intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin and Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir met Iranian leaders in Tehran on 26 October. A Saudi deputy minister said the aim was to reduce hostilities and support Qatari and Pakistani mediation; no outcome was announced.
  606. Oct 26 [moderate] Egypt's parliament authorised President Sisi to send military support to Saudi Arabia if Riyadh asks for it, by the two-thirds majority the constitution requires; Sisi says Egypt's role is limited to defending Saudi territory.
  607. Oct 26 [moderate] A Kuwaiti state security court sentenced three men to death for spying for Iran and Hezbollah and plotting to assassinate First Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef; the sentences can be appealed. On 28 October Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador over an embassy statement on the case.
  608. Oct 26 [moderate] An army strike on Tanqonj Market in Nyala, South Darfur, killed at least 102 people, AFP reports; the UN chief said on 31 October he was appalled by drone attacks on civilians in Sudan.
  609. Oct 27 [moderate] Turkey's parliamentary foreign affairs committee approved the Mecca defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a 16-article pact binding for ten years; it now goes to the full assembly, with no date set.
  610. Oct 27 [moderate] The Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire took effect on 27 October with no violations reported by either side; Russia said it halted strikes on Ukraine's Kherson, and Ukraine's negotiator Arakhamia said the truce runs to 1 November. An evacuation is planned.
  611. Oct 27 [moderate] Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones at Ukraine overnight into 27 October, hitting a Kyiv university campus and the Southern Bridge and killing one woman. Zelensky says Russia has fired more than 100 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv area since 14 October and Ukraine lacks Patriot interceptors while it waits for US sign-off.
  612. Oct 27 [moderate] The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on a Russian state investment fund, the New York Times reported on 27 October, citing an unnamed US official; no Treasury action has been published.
  613. Oct 27 [moderate] Russian satellites passed over Saudi oil and air-base sites before and after attacks by Iran-backed groups, AP reported, citing a private analysis firm and anonymous Saudi and Houthi officials. Russia did not comment; the claim rests on that analysis and unnamed sources.
  614. Oct 28 [high] The US told several Gulf states to prepare for a possible short but intense campaign against Iran after the 3 November midterms, the Wall Street Journal reported; Trump has not decided, and the White House says all options are on the table. An extra Patriot battery is moving to Israel.
  615. Oct 28 [moderate] Vice President Vance wrote to Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing a framework for negotiations, the Wall Street Journal reported; Trump said it was Vance's idea. A senior Iranian official called Qatar's latest ideas unacceptable.
  616. Oct 28 [moderate] US naval forces advised ships with no need to transit the Strait of Hormuz area to stay well clear, citing the geopolitical situation and blockade enforcement, in a notice issued through the Joint Maritime Information Center.
  617. Oct 28 [moderate] Three sea drones hit a Liberian-flagged container ship about 21 miles southeast of Shabla, in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone; all 18 crew were evacuated safely. Bulgaria named no attacker; Moscow denies involvement.
  618. Oct 28 [moderate] Houthi media said Saudi strikes killed 14 people at a market and petrol station in Yemen's Jawf province; Yemen's government said two Houthi ballistic missiles hit the perimeter of Aden airport, wounding civilians.
  619. Oct 28 [moderate] With about 86 percent of votes counted, Israeli broadcasters projected Netanyahu's bloc at 53 of 120 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc at 48, with Arab-majority parties at a record 19; Netanyahu stays caretaker prime minister during coalition talks.
  620. Oct 29 [moderate] North Korea fired around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area into the sea on 29 October; they flew about 250 km. Seoul called it a breach of UN resolutions amid a row over a border landmine blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers.
  621. Oct 29 [moderate] Russia said 613 Ukrainian drones were launched towards Moscow overnight into 29 October; Moscow's mayor said 231 were downed on approach to the city.
  622. Oct 29 [moderate] Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the timing of the next three-way talks with Ukraine and the US is linked to the Middle East conflict and does not allow a meeting in the near future; Zelensky had hoped for Abu Dhabi between 6 and 10 November.
  623. Oct 29 [moderate] UKMTO received a report of a ship on fire about nine nautical miles north of Oman's Khasab in the Strait of Hormuz; the cause and crew status were not given.
  624. Oct 29 [high] A small boat attached two limpet mines to the Panama-flagged tanker Louise 1 about 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, UKMTO and maritime security sources said; an engine-room fire disabled the ship; the crew is safe. gCaptain calls it the first reported limpet-mine hit on a merchant ship in this war.
  625. Oct 29 [high] Russian strikes killed at least 27 civilians and injured more than 140 across six Ukrainian regions on 29 October, Euromaidan Press tallied from regional reports; the Dnipro railway station toll reached 15, and Ukraine asked for an emergency UN Security Council meeting.
  626. Oct 29 [moderate] The Wall Street Journal reported that Ukraine agreed under US pressure to pause refinery strikes until after the midterms; Kyiv Independent sources say Ukraine never agreed, and one said Jared Kushner suggested a 30-day pause. Zelensky says no such order was given.
  627. Oct 29 [moderate] Drones struck the Jari 2 displacement camp near Hayk in Ethiopia's Amhara region, killing at least 15 people including five children; no party was named. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of sending troops across the border, and Eritrea calls that a declaration of war.
  628. Oct 29 [moderate] Israel's final results gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats, Gadi Eisenkot's opposition camp 48 and Arab parties a record 19; President Herzog will consult party leaders before giving anyone the mandate.
  629. Oct 29 [moderate] AFP heard at least eight explosions in Riyadh and the city issued a phone alert for a hostile aerial threat, later lifted; the Houthis said Saudi strikes killed 12 in Taiz province. Saudi officials confirmed neither.
  630. Oct 30 [high] The US State Department approved a possible $2.1 billion sale of 500 PAC-3 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, financed by Canada, Germany, Norway and EU-backed funds. Zelensky says deliveries may start only in years; Kyiv Post sources say after 2030.
  631. Oct 30 [moderate] NATO's top commander, US General Grynkewich, said weapons European allies paid for under the PURL scheme have been delivered, with a delivery in the last week and nothing delayed; he gave no types or numbers and did not address Zelensky's claim of a hold.
  632. Oct 30 [high] Evacuees left occupied Oleshky through Crimea, Anapa and four flights to Belarus, reaching Ukrainian-held territory on 31 October; no official total was given. Ukraine's ombudsman says neither side recorded a ceasefire violation.
  633. Oct 30 [moderate] The G20 foreign ministers' family photo in Atlanta was cancelled after about a third of the countries, including European states, the UK and Australia, refused to stand with Lavrov.
  634. Oct 30 [moderate] Pentagon officials have asked Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia to tone down their rhetoric on Russia, Reuters reports, citing four people familiar with the matter; Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby was among those involved. The Pentagon declined to comment.
  635. Oct 30 [moderate] The US is pressing Lithuania to allow Belarusian potash through Klaipeda despite EU sanctions, Politico reports via LRT; Lithuania's foreign minister says EU sanctions also forbid transit.
  636. Oct 30 [high] UKMTO reported a vessel hit by an unknown projectile about 40 nautical miles south of Lavan Island, causing a fire; the crew is safe. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy separately claimed four tankers on 'unauthorised routes' caught fire, which Reuters could not verify.
  637. Oct 30 [high] The Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda was struck in Gulf waters by what Qatar's state news agency called unidentified objects; there were no casualties and Qatar named no attacker.
  638. Oct 30 [moderate] Two missiles hit the presidential palace compound in Aden, a police official told AFP, without casualties; no one claimed it, and the official blamed the Houthis.
  639. Oct 30 [moderate] OCHA says more than 300,000 people displaced since March remain so in Lebanon, with Israeli demolitions, fires and strikes continuing in the south this week; about 970,000 have returned.
  640. Oct 30 [moderate] Lebanon's military court charged 13 people over a 780 kg explosives truck seized on the Beirut highway this month; Hezbollah said the explosives were its own and meant for Israeli forces in the south.
  641. Oct 30 [moderate] The UN rights office says Israeli deployment in Gaza is being expanded to 70 percent of the territory and that a 25 October drone strike on tents in Gaza City displaced about 800 people.
  642. Oct 30 [moderate] China expelled a record number of officials at the fifth plenum, among them 16 generals and former nuclear, aerospace and shipbuilding chiefs, SCMP reports; the purge reaches former theatre commanders.
  643. Oct 30 [moderate] Russian strikes left about 280,000 Ukrainian families without power, Zelensky said; drones hit Kyiv's water system, cutting supply across much of the city, according to Mayor Klitschko.
  644. Oct 31 [high] The FBI said North Korea was responsible for stealing more than $6 billion from Binance, naming the TraderTraitor group and saying the assets are being laundered into Ethereum. Trump said 'we don't know if it's North Korea'; Binance says it replaced 90 percent and is resuming withdrawals.
  645. Oct 31 [high] Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei told commanders any threat must meet an 'immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response' and ordered the target list updated; Rubio said Trump has not decided on new strikes.
  646. Oct 31 [high] Trump said the US still has to 'take care of one or two' sites in Iran, naming Pickaxe Mountain, and spoke to Netanyahu, the WSJ reports; MSNOW says Gulf officials were warned of strikes as early as 4 November. Trump says he is in no hurry.
  647. Oct 31 [moderate] Iranian and Qatari envoys held more than 12 hours of talks in Tehran and met again in Doha, Reuters reports. Security chief Rezaei says Vance's letter changed the US tone, but Iran will not reopen Hormuz or negotiate until its seven conditions are met.
  648. Oct 31 [moderate] A US delegation is expected to join indirect Iran talks in Doha with no arrival date set, The New Arab reports, citing mediators and Axios; Foreign Minister Araghchi says no meetings with Americans are planned.
  649. Oct 31 [high] Oman's Maritime Security Centre said its navy rescued 25 crew from the Panama-flagged tanker Riti after it was targeted and caught fire; Iran's Guard says it halted three tankers on an 'unauthorised route'.
  650. Oct 31 [moderate] Rubio said in Atlanta he does not know whether a negotiated peace in Ukraine is achievable; Kyiv Post, citing a Radio Liberty correspondent and European officials, says he doubts Putin will settle before spring 2027.
  651. Oct 31 [moderate] The US Embassy warned of a credible threat of a 'mass casualty event' at the Tsaritsyno palace park in Moscow and told people to stay away; Russia's FSB said it received the warning, according to TASS.
  652. Oct 31 [moderate] Erdogan told Zelensky in Istanbul that attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea are unacceptable whoever carries them out; Ankara's proposal to end such strikes has not been taken up.
  653. Oct 31 [moderate] Syria's foreign minister confirmed Damascus is discussing joining the Mecca defence pact of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, giving no timeline.
  654. Oct 31 [moderate] North Korean state media KCNA said the country tested a Standard Type 2 cluster-bomb warhead on Hwasong-11D missiles, claiming it can destroy 12 to 13 hectares and that units will field four warhead types this year; the claim is unverified.
  655. Oct 31 [moderate] China's coast guard announced a new patrol off Taiwan's east coast with two ships and sent another near Pratas; Taiwan's coast guard says China is harassing shipping by radio and claiming a fictional jurisdiction.
  656. Oct 31 [moderate] Quad foreign ministers voiced grave concern about overcapacity and finalised a leaders' summit in the Philippines next month, weeks before Trump meets Xi in Shenzhen, SCMP reports; Rubio says the group is not anti-China but that the behaviours come from one country.
  657. Nov 1 [moderate] Ukrainian drones struck the Lukoil refinery and an adjacent power plant in Kstovo overnight, starting major fires, after hits on a Bashneft plant in Ufa and a rocket-fuel plant in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky.
  658. Nov 2 [critical] The US struck Iranian surface-to-air missile sites on Qeshm and Hengam islands near Bandar Abbas late on 2 November, a US official told AP and Euronews, describing them as defensive; Iranian state media reported explosions and no casualties.
  659. Nov 2 [critical] A Russian strike on a school used as an aid point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, killed at least 31 people, with about 50 missing, regional officials say; Russia's defence ministry says it hit Ukrainian troops.
  660. Nov 2 [high] Houthi forces advanced to within about 80 km of Aden, taking Al-Maqatirah district and fighting at the entrance to Tur al-Bahah, Reuters reports, citing four military sources; the Taiz-Aden road has been cut since early October.
  661. Nov 3 [high] The Indian-flagged dhow Al-Jusufi was hit by what India's shipping minister called an unidentified aerial object near Limah in Omani waters; one Indian crewman died and Oman's coast guard rescued 13. India says 15 Indian seafarers have been killed near Hormuz since March.
  662. Nov 3 [high] Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterms, with at least 54 Senate seats per Al Jazeera; Trump said the Iran war and petrol prices played a part, but that the war decision was right.
  663. Nov 3 [critical] Russia launched its largest attack on Ukraine's energy system this year, 289 drones, 17 ballistic and 59 cruise missiles per energy minister Shmyhal; a substation serving the Khmelnytskyi nuclear plant was hit, and Kyiv faced power cuts and water outages.
  664. Nov 3 [high] The White House said the US will mediate working-level talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November, the first three-way talks since February; the Kremlin confirmed and is sending Vladimir Medinsky again.
  665. Nov 5 [high] One seafarer was killed when the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Velos Sapphire was hit in the Gulf, probably by a missile, while sailing empty toward Bahrain, its Greek manager told Reuters; the attacker was not identified.
  666. Nov 5 [high] Turkey's parliament approved the Mecca defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan by 279 votes to 119; the pact treats an attack on one as an attack on all, but sending Turkish troops needs a separate vote.
  667. Nov 5 [high] Trump met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev privately at the White House and said a coming deal 'might involve all of Europe'; Kushner listed five aims for a European security framework but announced no agreement.
  668. Nov 5 [high] A Helsinki court jailed the Russian captain and an Azerbaijani crew member of the cargo ship Fitburg for aggravated sabotage after it dragged its anchor about 130 km and cut two Finland-Estonia cables last year.
  669. Nov 6 [critical] Trump confirmed new 'minor' US strikes on an Iranian air-defence site on Qeshm island, saying 'we knocked it out in about 15 minutes'; Iranian state media reported two missile impacts in the Suza area. CENTCOM gave no on-record comment.
  670. Nov 6 [high] Saudi air defences shot down two ballistic missiles aimed at Najran and a drone over Makkah region on 6 November and a cruise missile aimed at Riyadh early on 7 November, the coalition spokesman said; no casualties were reported.
  671. Nov 6 [high] EU foreign policy chief Kallas said in Warsaw the EU will not implement any US-Russia agreement it is not party to; Poland's and Ukraine's foreign ministers agreed, and Zelensky said 'we don't want Yalta 2.0'.
  672. Nov 7 [high] Regional officials told Reuters a Qatari bridge plan would have the US lift its blockade and release some frozen funds while Iran admits IAEA inspectors, then reopen Hormuz on day two; Iran is reviewing it and the White House declined comment.
  673. Nov 7 [critical] Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and its region overnight, Zelensky said, closing the Northern Bridge and and, he said, hitting substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants to Kyiv; at least six were injured in Kyiv, and police reported one death in the region.

Conflict arcs

Trump calls Iran war 'effectively over' as US enforces blockade

Epic Fury · Lead Development

Trump said on 9 November, after meeting Qatar's prime minister, that the war is 'militarily effectively over' and further strikes are 'quite unlikely'. Rubio reported no progress in talks. US aircraft disabled a cargo ship running the blockade off Khor Fakkan, and the US moved tankers out of a British base over an Iranian threat.

What changed

Washington's message shifted from strikes to economic pressure: Trump now calls more strikes unlikely, while the blockade is enforced at sea and a new task force targets land routes. Talks have not moved, by Rubio's account. Iran's confrontation with the West widened beyond the Gulf, with France attributing cyber sabotage to the Guard and the US moving aircraft from a British base over an Iranian threat. The Guard again claims tankers hit mines; none is confirmed.

What to watch

Whether Iran answers Qatar or a US delegation joins talks; any further US strike despite Trump's remarks; more blockade interceptions; France's response and any EU listing; the threat behind the Mildenhall move; confirmation of the Guard's tanker claims.

China extends US trade truce as Trump eyes three-leader meeting

US-BRICS Rivalry · Lead Development

China extended its trade truce with the US by two months, keeping a 24% tariff suspended and critical-mineral export waivers in place to 10 January. Trump says he expects to meet Putin and Xi at APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November. France blamed Iran's Guard for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges.

What changed

The economic cliff of 10 November passed without a fight: Beijing rolled over every suspended measure for two months, citing the Washington summit. The three-leader meeting moved from Chinese hints to Trump saying he expects it. In Europe, Iran joined Russia as a named source of cyber sabotage, and US forces moved aircraft out of a British base. Lithuania opened talks on renaming Taiwan's office, a reversal of its 2021 stance.

What to watch

Whether the White House or Beijing confirms a Shenzhen meeting with Putin; APEC on 18-19 November; the Quad summit in Manila; China's response to the Nvidia spy case; Lithuania's talks with Chinese diplomats; North Korean launches.

Russia and Ukraine open US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi

Russia-Ukraine · Lead Development

Russian and Ukrainian delegations sat down with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, the first such talks in nine months. US officials say they want a 'final end' and a new Russia-Europe security architecture. A drone killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, the IAEA said.

What changed

The three sides are in one room for the first time since February, and the US agenda is wider than Ukraine: officials describe a security architecture for Russia and Europe and say sanctions relief could be part of a deal. Europe is present in Abu Dhabi but outside the core format, and France says European security cannot be negotiated before a ceasefire. Russia kept striking power plants before the talks.

What to watch

Whether the talks produce any ceasefire terms, including energy or maritime; whether a European joins a session with Russia; US moves on sanctions relief; another mass missile strike; the Zaporizhzhia plant's power supply.
